defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7154Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7154 — Auto-charge the card on file

  Job completion and invoice generation are covered end-to-end by
  criterion 7153's own spec. This spec's subject is the
  charge-the-card-on-file decision, so the completed job and its
  invoice are seeded directly via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` rather
  than re-driving completion here.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "charging the client's card on file for a generated invoice" do
    scenario "auto-charge the card on file" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client has a valid card on file", context do
        client =
          Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{
            card_on_file: true,
            card_token: "pm_card_visa"
          })

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client, client)}
      end

      given_ "the invoice is generated for a completed job", context do
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, context.client)
        invoice = Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{amount: job.agreed_price})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the owner charges the card on file", context do
        {:ok, invoice_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        invoice_live
        |> element("[data-test='charge-card-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :invoice_live, invoice_live)}
      end

      then_ "the card is charged for the invoice amount", context do
        assert render(context.invoice_live) =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client receives a receipt", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7190Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7190 — Moving a job's time on the schedule board pushes the
  reassigned cleaner a notification describing the old and new times.

  Assumes the board exposes a per-job start-time control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-start-time-input']`, `phx-change="reschedule_job"`)
  alongside the cleaner-select control already assumed by story 834's
  criterion 7170.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a moved job notifies the assigned cleaner" do
    scenario "moved job notifies the cleaner" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I am a cleaner with a job scheduled today at 1:00 PM", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[14:30:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the office moves that job to 3:00 PM", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-start-time-input']")
        |> render_change(%{"start_time" => "15:00"})

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I receive a notification describing the change from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM", context do
        {:ok, today_live, html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        assert has_element?(today_live, "[data-test='schedule-alert']")
        assert html =~ "1:00 PM"
        assert html =~ "3:00 PM"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  # `account_fixture/2` creates the account, so it never carries an
  # `active_account_id` — every fixture below that scopes a context
  # call by account needs to resolve it from the user's membership at
  # call time instead of trusting the scope it was handed.
  defp scoped_to_account(%CleanerCrm.Users.Scope{active_account_id: nil, user: user} = scope) do
    case CleanerCrm.Accounts.MembersRepository.list_user_accounts(user.id) do
      [account | _] -> %{scope | active_account_id: account.id, active_account: account}
      [] -> scope
    end
  end

  defp scoped_to_account(scope), do: scope

  # Two hours after `start_time`, unless that would wrap past midnight
  # (into an earlier clock time), in which case the day just ends there.
  defp default_end_time(start_time) do
    candidate = Time.add(start_time, 2 * 3600, :second)
    if Time.compare(candidate, start_time) == :gt, do: candidate, else: ~T[23:59:59]
  end

  def job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(scope, client, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)
    job = job_fixture(scope, client, Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :completed}))

    {:ok, _checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{
          task: "Kitchen counters wiped down",
          before_photo: "before_kitchen.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_kitchen.jpg"
        },
        %{
          task: "Bathrooms sanitized",
          before_photo: "before_bath.jpg",
          after_photo: "after_bath.jpg"
        }
      ])

    job
  end

  def invoice_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, invoice} =
      CleanerCrm.Billing.create_invoice(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          amount: job.agreed_price,
          status: :unpaid
        })
      )

    invoice
  end

  # Time tracking (story 838) — a resolved clock-in/out record for a
  # job.
  #
  # Clocking in and out through the UI is covered end-to-end by story
  # 838's own "cleaner clocks in and out of an assigned job" spec
  # (drives FieldLive.Job). Scenarios whose subject is a downstream pay
  # calculation (hourly vs. piece-rate, running pay-period totals,
  # payroll CSV export) seed the resolved time entry directly here
  # instead of re-driving the clock-in/out flow every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def time_entry_fixture(scope, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, time_entry} =
      CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.create_time_entry(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          job_id: job.id,
          clocked_in_at: ~U[2024-01-08 09:00:00Z],
          clocked_out_at: ~U[2024-01-08 12:00:00Z]
        })
      )

    time_entry
  end

  # Notifications (story 837) — an already-sent appointment reminder
  # with its confirm/reschedule token.
  #
  # The automatic "reminder sent at the configured lead time" trigger
  # is covered end-to-end by story 837's own "reminder fires at the
  # configured lead time" spec. Scenarios whose subject is a
  # downstream decision on an existing reminder (confirm, reschedule,
  # delivery-status fallback) seed the already-sent notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the scheduler trigger every
  # time — a sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md.
  def notification_fixture(scope, client, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          client_id: client.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :reminder,
          channel: :email,
          status: :sent,
          token: "reminder_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Schedule alerts (story 843) — a pending schedule-change
  # notification already pushed to a cleaner.
  #
  # The push itself (a moved or cancelled job creating this
  # notification) is covered end-to-end by story 843's own "moved job
  # notifies the cleaner" / "cancelled job notifies the cleaner"
  # specs, which drive the real trigger via `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  # Scenarios whose subject is a downstream decision on an existing
  # pending change (acknowledging, re-prompting, office visibility,
  # escalation, channel fallback) seed the already-pushed notification
  # directly here instead of re-driving the board move every time — a
  # sanctioned shortcut per bdd/spex/boundaries.md. Never pass
  # `status: :acknowledged` here — the acknowledgment round-trip
  # through `FieldLive.Today` is the whole point of story 843.
  def schedule_change_notification_fixture(scope, cleaner, job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    {:ok, notification} =
      CleanerCrm.Notifications.create_notification(
        scoped_to_account(scope),
        Enum.into(attrs, %{
          cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
          job_id: job.id,
          kind: :schedule_change,
          channel: :push,
          status: :pending,
          change_summary: "Job schedule changed",
          pushed_at: DateTime.utc_now(),
          token: "schedule_change_token_#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}"
        })
      )

    notification
  end

  # Quality (story 839) — a job carrying an unfinished, per-job
  # checklist of required and optional tasks.
  #
  # Checking items off and completing the job through the checklist UI
  # is the subject under test in `FieldLive.Job`, so this fixture stops
  # short of that — it only seeds the checklist itself. Sanctioned
  # bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md: `ChecklistTemplate` assignment
  # (story 842) has its own creation flow this fixture skips.
  def job_with_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} =
      CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, [
        %{task: "Kitchen counters wiped down", required: true},
        %{task: "Bathrooms sanitized", required: true},
        %{task: "Fridge interior wiped down", required: false}
      ])

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end

  # Quality (story 842) — a job carrying an unfinished, room-grouped
  # checklist whose items are exactly what the caller passes in.
  #
  # Story 842 owns the `ChecklistTemplate` -> per-job `Checklist`
  # assignment flow (which room/task combinations count as in scope for
  # a given job). That assignment UI doesn't exist yet and isn't part
  # of this story's component list (only `FieldLive.ChecklistComponent`
  # is), so seeding the already-instantiated, room-tagged checklist
  # directly is the sanctioned bypass per bdd/spex/boundaries.md — the
  # subject under test is opening/working the checklist on
  # `FieldLive.Job`, not how it got assigned. `items` is a list of
  # `%{room:, task:, required:}` maps; a spec proving an out-of-scope
  # task never appears simply omits it from `items`.
  def job_with_room_checklist_fixture(scope, client, cleaner, items, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope = scoped_to_account(scope)

    job =
      job_fixture(
        scope,
        client,
        Enum.into(attrs, %{status: :in_progress, cleaner_id: cleaner.id})
      )

    {:ok, checklist} = CleanerCrm.Quality.create_checklist(scope, job, items)

    %{job: job, checklist: checklist}
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrmWeb.Router do
  use CleanerCrmWeb, :router

  import CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth

  pipeline :browser do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_live_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :protect_from_forgery
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :api do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # No `:protect_from_forgery` — unlike the GET-only public routes below
  # (which can just use `:browser`), `/pay/:token` accepts a POST from a
  # client with no session and no CSRF token (a mailed or shared link).
  # `:fetch_current_scope_for_user` still runs — the root layout reads
  # `@current_scope` unconditionally, and this plug assigns `nil` when
  # no one's logged in rather than requiring an authenticated visitor.
  pipeline :public do
    plug :accepts, ["html"]
    plug :fetch_session
    plug :fetch_flash
    plug :put_root_layout, html: {CleanerCrmWeb.Layouts, :root}
    plug :put_secure_browser_headers
    plug :fetch_current_scope_for_user
  end

  pipeline :webhook do
    plug :accepts, ["json"]
  end

  # Office-only controller routes (e.g. the payroll CSV export) layer
  # this on top of `:require_authenticated_user`; office-only
  # LiveViews use the equivalent `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole`
  # on_mount hook instead, since a plug can't gate a live_session.
  pipeline :require_office_role do
    plug CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :browser

    get "/", PageController, :home
  end

  # Other scopes may use custom stacks.
  # scope "/api", CleanerCrmWeb do
  #   pipe_through :api
  # end

  # Enable LiveDashboard and Swoosh mailbox preview in development
  if Application.compile_env(:cleaner_crm, :dev_routes) do
    # If you want to use the LiveDashboard in production, you should put
    # it behind authentication and allow only admins to access it.
    # If your application does not have an admins-only section yet,
    # you can use Plug.BasicAuth to set up some basic authentication
    # as long as you are also using SSL (which you should anyway).
    import Phoenix.LiveDashboard.Router

    scope "/dev" do
      pipe_through :browser

      live_dashboard "/dashboard", metrics: CleanerCrmWeb.Telemetry
      forward "/mailbox", Plug.Swoosh.MailboxPreview
    end
  end

  ## Authentication routes

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    live_session :require_authenticated_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated}] do
      live "/users/settings", UserLive.Settings, :edit
      live "/users/settings/confirm-email/:token", UserLive.Settings, :confirm_email

      live "/accounts", AccountLive.Index, :index
      live "/accounts/new", AccountLive.Form, :new
      live "/accounts/:id/edit", AccountLive.Form, :edit
      live "/accounts/picker", AccountLive.Picker, :index
      live "/accounts/:id", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/manage", AccountLive.Manage, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/members", AccountLive.Members, :show
      live "/accounts/:id/invitations", AccountLive.Invitations, :show

      live "/integrations", IntegrationLive.Index, :index

      live "/field", FieldLive.Today, :index
      live "/field/jobs/:id", FieldLive.Job, :show
    end

    # Office-only surfaces: dispatch, payroll, quality, invoicing,
    # clients, quotes, reminders, and the audit trail. Gated to
    # owners/admins by `CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole` — a cleaner
    # is redirected to `/field` instead. See that module for why it's
    # a separate `live_session` from the one above.
    live_session :require_office_role,
      on_mount: [
        {CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :require_authenticated},
        {CleanerCrmWeb.RequireOfficeRole, :default}
      ] do
      live "/clients", ClientLive.Index, :index
      live "/clients/new", ClientLive.Index, :new
      live "/clients/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit
      live "/clients/:id/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_client_property
      live "/clients/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show
      live "/properties/new", ClientLive.Show, :new_property
      live "/properties/:id/edit", ClientLive.Show, :edit_property
      live "/properties/:id", ClientLive.Show, :show_property

      live "/schedule", ScheduleLive.Index, :index
      live "/schedule/plans/new", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :new
      live "/schedule/plans/:id/edit", ScheduleLive.PlanLive, :edit
      live "/schedule/jobs/new", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :new
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id/assign", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :assign
      live "/schedule/jobs/:id", ScheduleLive.JobLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/new", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :new
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:id", ScheduleLive.CleanerLive, :show
      live "/schedule/cleaners/:cleaner_id/time-off/new", ScheduleLive.AvailabilityLive, :new

      live "/audit", AuditLive, :index

      live "/quotes", QuoteLive.Index, :index
      live "/quotes/new", QuoteLive.Builder, :new
      live "/quotes/:id", QuoteLive.Builder, :show

      live "/quality", QualityLive.Review, :index
      live "/quality/scorecards", QualityLive.Scorecards, :index
      live "/quality/templates", QualityLive.Templates, :index
      live "/quality/templates/new", QualityLive.Templates, :new
      live "/quality/templates/:id/edit", QualityLive.Templates, :edit
      live "/quality/:job_id", QualityLive.Review, :show

      live "/timesheets", TimesheetLive, :index

      live "/invoices", InvoiceLive.Index, :index
      live "/invoices/:id", InvoiceLive.Show, :show

      live "/reminders", ReminderLive, :index
    end

    post "/users/update-password", UserSessionController, :update_password
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user, :require_office_role]

    get "/timesheets/export", TimesheetExportController, :show
  end

  scope "/integrations/oauth", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

    get "/:provider", IntegrationsController, :request
    get "/callback/:provider", IntegrationsController, :callback
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through [:browser]

    live_session :current_user,
      on_mount: [{CleanerCrmWeb.UserAuth, :mount_current_scope}] do
      live "/users/register", UserLive.Registration, :new
      live "/users/log-in", UserLive.Login, :new
      live "/users/log-in/:token", UserLive.Confirmation, :new
      live "/invitations/accept/:token", InvitationsLive.Accept, :new
    end

    post "/users/log-in", UserSessionController, :create
    delete "/users/log-out", UserSessionController, :delete

    # Public confirm/reschedule links a client reaches from their
    # reminder — no login, so `:browser` (not `:require_authenticated_user`)
    # like the routes above. Plain `:browser`, not `:public`, so
    # `fetch_current_scope_for_user` still assigns `current_scope` for
    # the root layout.
    get "/reminders/confirm/:token", ReminderController, :confirm
    get "/reminders/reschedule/:token", ReminderController, :reschedule
  end

  scope "/", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :public

    get "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :show
    post "/pay/:token", PaymentController, :create
  end

  scope "/webhooks", CleanerCrmWeb do
    pipe_through :webhook

    post "/stripe", StripeWebhookController, :create
    post "/twilio", TwilioWebhookController, :status
  end
end

## Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy (ID: 851)

As a cleaning client, I want to reschedule or cancel an upcoming visit from the portal within the company's stated notice policy (with any late fee shown before I confirm), so that I stay in control without phone tag and the company isn't blindsided. (Research: self-service reschedule/cancel within a 24–48h policy is the expectation; captured policy agreement prevents disputes — customer-side.md §1)

**Acceptance Criteria:** 7 total, 0 verified

- [ ] Client reschedules a visit from the portal (criterion 7222)
- [ ] Late cancellation shows fee before confirming (criterion 7223)
- [ ] On-time cancellation has no fee (criterion 7224)
- [ ] Reschedule notifies office and cleaner (criterion 7225)
- [ ] Reschedule preserves price and scope (criterion 7226)
- [ ] Cannot modify a completed visit (criterion 7227)
- [ ] Same-day cancellation charges the maximum fee (criterion 7229)

As a cleaning client, I want to view and pay invoices in the portal, manage my card on file, and add a digital tip that reaches my cleaner, so that payment never needs a phone call and tipping doesn't need cash. (Research: over half of tips are digital and incumbents track tips poorly — an in-portal tip prompt is a customer convenience and a cleaner-retention lever — customer-side.md §1; owner-side payment pains pain-points §1.8)

- [ ] Client saves a card on file (criterion 7241)
- [ ] Client adds a tip at payment (criterion 7242)

## Leave a review when the job is done well (ID: 853)

As a cleaning client, I want a thank-you note after my cleaning with a low-friction review prompt (and a private complaint path if I'm unhappy), so that praising a great cleaner is effortless and problems reach the owner before they reach Google. (Research: Housecall Pro's auto thank-you + ~24h delayed review request is its single most-praised cleaning feature, yielding 2–3x review growth — customer-side.md §4)

**Acceptance Criteria:** 7 total, 0 verified

- [ ] Thank-you sent on job completion (criterion 7244)
- [ ] Review request sent ~24h after completion (criterion 7245)
- [ ] No duplicate review request (criterion 7246)
- [ ] High rating routes to publish (criterion 7247)
- [ ] Low rating routes to private complaint (criterion 7248)
- [ ] Owner receives private complaint (criterion 7249)
- [ ] No review prompt for incomplete visit (criterion 7250)

**Story ID**: 851
**Description**: As a cleaning client, I want to reschedule or cancel an upcoming visit from the portal within the company's stated notice policy (with any late fee shown before I confirm), so that I stay in control without phone tag and the company isn't blindsided. (Research: self-service reschedule/cancel within a 24–48h policy is the expectation; captured policy agreement prevents disputes — customer-side.md §1)
**Component**: `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive` (live_context)

## What you're producing

These are specifications of acceptance criteria, not regression tests
of existing behavior. A scenario is a mechanical translation of the
criterion text into Given/When/Then driving the real surface — what
the criterion **says must be true**, not what the code happens to do
today.

**Failing on first run is the expected outcome.** Unsatisfied criteria
produce red specs; the next workflow step uses that red bar to drive
the implementation. You do **not** need the scenarios to pass for
this task to succeed.

**The evaluator is shape-only** — it parses, compiles, asserts
`use *.Spex.Case`, and asserts Given/When/Then steps exist. It does
**not** run `mix test`. Validation passing is not the same as
scenarios passing. Encode the criterion faithfully; let the implementer
worry about turning it green.

## Required reading — both layers

Read both knowledge layers before writing specs. **Project rules
override framework rules where they conflict.**

### Framework BDD knowledge (read via the `read_knowledge` MCP tool, under `bdd/spex/`)

- `bdd/spex/writing_a_spex.md` — file layout, module template, DSL
  syntax, step return values. **Essential — read first.**

  regular tests.
- `bdd/spex/environment.md` — environment abstraction in steps.

  can't do.
- `bdd/spex/shared_givens.md` — importing shared given blocks.
- `bdd/spex/recording_cassettes.md` — when and how to record HTTP
  cassettes.

### Project BDD knowledge (`.code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/`)

  in this codebase (MCP tool, HTTP, LiveView, filesystem) with
  one-line "I'm testing X → use surface Y" table and 30-second
  skeletons. **Read second.**
- `surfaces.md` — canonical skeletons per surface, deeper detail.
- `cassettes.md` — project-specific cassette conventions.

  and criteria already on the story. If something feels

  fail.** A failing scenario is the point. Tagging it out hides the
  signal the implementer needs.
- **Pre-seed in `given_` what the SUT should produce.** If the
  criterion says "creating a Foo also creates a Bar", `when_`
  triggers the action and `then_` asserts both side effects.
  Don't `given_` the Bar into existence.
- **Stub or mock the surface under test.** Drive the real LiveView /
  HTTP / MCP tool. Mocks make the spec a tautology.
- **Read the implementation and write its current behavior as the
  expectation.** Read the criterion; write the criterion. If the
  code doesn't match, that's information — surface it through a
  failing spec.

If a criterion is genuinely untestable, contradicts another, or is
ambiguous, **stop and flag it** rather than fudging the spec to fit.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens do
  @moduledoc """
  Shared givens for Cleaner CRM BDD specs.

  Consumer spex modules pull these in with a plain Elixir `import`:

      import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

      scenario "..." do
        given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account
      end

  | Name | Produces | Requires |
  |---|---|---|
  | `:logged_in_owner_with_account` | `context.conn` (authenticated), `context.user`, `context.scope`, `context.account` | `context.conn` |
  """

  use SexySpex.Givens

  import Phoenix.ConnTest
  import Phoenix.LiveViewTest

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

  register_given :logged_in_owner_with_account, context do
    user = Fixtures.user_fixture() |> Fixtures.set_password()
    scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
    account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

    {:ok, login_live, _html} = live(context.conn, "/users/log-in")

    form =
      form(login_live, "#login_form_password",
        user: %{
          email: user.email,
          password: Fixtures.valid_user_password(),
          remember_me: true
        }
      )

    conn = submit_form(form, context.conn)

    {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
  end
end

# BDD Spec Plan — Cleaner CRM

How BDD specs work in *this* project. The framework docs
(`philosophy.md`, `boundaries.md`, `writing_a_spex.md` in the harness
knowledge base) cover the generic rules; this file names the concrete
surfaces, fixtures, and anti-patterns for Cleaner CRM.

## Public surfaces a spec may drive

Specs act through LiveView routes (via `Phoenix.LiveViewTest`) and the
public controllers. Concretely:

**Office/admin side (owner persona):**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ClientLive.*` — `/clients`, client + property + access management (story 832)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Board` — `/schedule`, weekly dispatch board (833, 834, 846)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.QuoteLive.*` — `/quotes`, quote builder (835)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.*` — `/invoices` (836)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive` — reminder settings + delivery log (837)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.TimesheetLive` — time review + payroll export (838)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.QualityLive.*` — job review + scorecards (839)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.AuditLive` — audit trail (840)

**Cleaner field side (cleaner persona):**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Today` — day view + change alerts (841, 843)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.FieldLive.Job` — checklist, photos, clock in/out, incident reports (842, 844, 845)

**Public (unauthenticated) surfaces:**
- `CleanerCrmWeb.PaymentController` — payment-link pages (836)
- `CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderController` — reminder confirm/reschedule links (837)
- Auth: `/users/register`, `/users/log-in` LiveViews (generated)

## Fixture inventory (`CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures`)

- `user_fixture/1` — confirmed user (owner/office/cleaner depending on attrs)
- `unconfirmed_user_fixture/1` — pre-confirmation user for auth specs
- `user_scope_fixture/0,1` — scope wrapping a user, for seeding deeper state
- `valid_user_password/0`, `set_password/1` — password login in specs
- `account_fixture/2` — a company (tenant) owned by the given scope

Grow this list only when a spec's `given_` needs state whose creation
flow is covered by another spec. Every addition is a sanctioned bypass.

## Legal observable surfaces in `then_`

- LiveView render assertions: `assert render(view) =~ "Job scheduled"`
- LiveView navigation: `assert_patch/2`, `assert_redirect/2`
- Flash content via rendered layout
- Controller responses: `html_response(conn, 200)`, redirects on payment/reminder links
- Email delivery via `Swoosh.TestAssertions` (reminder + invitation emails)
- NOT legal: asserting on Repo rows, context return values, or PubSub
  messages via direct `assert_receive` on internals — observe what a
  user (or webhook peer) can observe.

## Project-specific anti-patterns

- Do not seed `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` jobs in `given_` by calling the
  context — the covered creation flow is the ScheduleLive board / plan
  form. If a spec needs "a scheduled job" as a precondition, either
  drive the UI in `given_` steps or add a sanctioned fixture here first.
- Do not flip `Notification` acknowledgment state directly — the whole
  point of story 843 is the acknowledgment round-trip through
  `FieldLive.Today`.
- Do not stub time by editing rows; recurrence/conflict scenarios pin
  wall-clock via plan dates chosen in the future.
- External HTTP (Stripe, Twilio, Resend, S3) is always cassette- or
  adapter-faked; a spec must never hit a live API.

- `unconfirmed_user_fixture/1` — pre-confirmation user for auth specs
- `user_scope_fixture/0,1` — scope wrapping a user, for seeding deeper state
- `valid_user_password/0`, `set_password/1` — password login in specs
- `account_fixture/2` — a company (tenant) owned by the given scope

Grow this list only when a spec's `given_` needs state whose creation
flow is covered by another spec. Every addition is a sanctioned bypass.

## Legal observable surfaces in `then_`

- LiveView render assertions: `assert render(view) =~ "Job scheduled"`
- LiveView navigation: `assert_patch/2`, `assert_redirect/2`
- Flash content via rendered layout
- Controller responses: `html_response(conn, 200)`, redirects on payment/reminder links
- Email delivery via `Swoosh.TestAssertions` (reminder + invitation emails)
- NOT legal: asserting on Repo rows, context return values, or PubSub
  messages via direct `assert_receive` on internals — observe what a
  user (or webhook peer) can observe.

## Project-specific anti-patterns

- Do not seed `CleanerCrm.Scheduling` jobs in `given_` by calling the
  context — the covered creation flow is the ScheduleLive board / plan
  form. If a spec needs "a scheduled job" as a precondition, either
  drive the UI in `given_` steps or add a sanctioned fixture here first.
- Do not flip `Notification` acknowledgment state directly — the whole
  point of story 843 is the acknowledgment round-trip through
  `FieldLive.Today`.
- Do not stub time by editing rows; recurrence/conflict scenarios pin
  wall-clock via plan dates chosen in the future.
- External HTTP (Stripe, Twilio, Resend, S3) is always cassette- or
  adapter-faked; a spec must never hit a live API.

## Get an instant quote from the public website (ID: 848)

As a cleaning client, I want a public instant-quote form (bedrooms, bathrooms, square footage, frequency, add-ons) that shows me a real price from the company's rate card before I hand over contact details, so that I can decide in one sitting instead of waiting for a callback I may never answer. (Research: instant-quote booking forms are the residential standard and convert where request-a-quote friction loses time-pressured jobs — customer-side.md §1, §3)

**Acceptance Criteria:** 7 total, 0 verified

- [ ] Building a quote with room counts shows a price with no contact info (criterion 7215)
- [ ] Building a quote by square footage instead of room counts (criterion 7216)
- [ ] Changing any input recomputes the total live (criterion 7217)
- [ ] Selecting bi-weekly frequency applies the recurring discount (criterion 7218)
- [ ] Selecting add-ons increases the running total (criterion 7219)
- [ ] Unsupported input combination shows a message instead of a wrong price (criterion 7220)
- [ ] Instant quote price matches the later acceptance total (criterion 7221)

defmodule CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase do
  @moduledoc """
  This module defines the test case to be used by
  tests that require setting up a connection.

  Such tests rely on `Phoenix.ConnTest` and also
  import other functionality to make it easier
  to build common data structures and query the data layer.

  Finally, if the test case interacts with the database,
  we enable the SQL sandbox, so changes done to the database
  are reverted at the end of every test. If you are using
  PostgreSQL, you can even run database tests asynchronously
  by setting `use CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase, async: true`, although
  this option is not recommended for other databases.
  """

  use ExUnit.CaseTemplate

  using do
    quote do
      # The default endpoint for testing
      @endpoint CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint

      use CleanerCrmWeb, :verified_routes

      # Import conveniences for testing with connections
      import Plug.Conn
      import Phoenix.ConnTest
      import CleanerCrmTest.ConnCase
    end
  end

  setup tags do
    CleanerCrmTest.DataCase.setup_sandbox(tags)
    {:ok, conn: Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()}
  end

  @doc """
  Setup helper that registers and logs in users.

      setup :register_and_log_in_user

  It stores an updated connection and a registered user in the
  test context.
  """
  def register_and_log_in_user(%{conn: conn} = context) do
    user = CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.user_fixture()
    scope = CleanerCrm.Users.Scope.for_user(user)

    opts =
      context
      |> Map.take([:token_authenticated_at])
      |> Enum.into([])

    %{conn: log_in_user(conn, user, opts), user: user, scope: scope}
  end

  @doc """
  Logs the given `user` into the `conn`.

  It returns an updated `conn`.
  """
  def log_in_user(conn, user, opts \\ []) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Users.generate_user_session_token(user)

    maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, opts[:token_authenticated_at])

    conn
    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:user_token, token)
  end

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(_token, nil), do: nil

  defp maybe_set_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at) do
    CleanerCrm.UsersFixtures.override_token_authenticated_at(token, authenticated_at)
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
4	  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
5	  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
6	  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.
7	
8	  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
9	  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
10	  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
11	  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
12	  """
13	
14	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
15	
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
17	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
18	
19	  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
20	    Notification,
21	    ReminderNotifier,
22	    ReminderScheduler,
23	    ReminderSettings
24	  }
25	
26	  ## Reminder settings
27	
28	  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
29	  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
31	      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
32	      settings -> settings
33	    end
34	  end
35	
36	  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
37	    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
38	  end
39	
40	  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
41	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
42	    scope
43	    |> get_reminder_settings()
44	    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
45	    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
46	  end
47	
48	  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
49	  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send
50	
51	  ## Notifications
52	
53	  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
54	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
55	    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
56	    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
57	    |> Repo.insert()
58	  end
59	
60	  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
61	  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
62	    Notification
63	    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
64	    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
65	    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
66	    |> Repo.all()
67	  end
68	
69	  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available
70	
71	  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
72	    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
73	  end
74	
75	  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
76	    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
77	      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
78	    else
79	      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
80	    end
81	  end
82	
83	  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
84	    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
85	      update_status(notification,
86	        status: :reschedule_requested,
87	        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
88	      )
89	    else
90	      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
91	    end
92	  end
93	
94	  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
95	  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
96	    Notification
97	    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
98	    |> Repo.exists?()
99	  end
100	
101	  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
102	  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
103	    Notification
104	    |> where(
105	      [n],
106	      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
107	    )
108	    |> Repo.exists?()
109	  end
110	
111	  @doc """
112	  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
113	  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
114	  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
115	  `:reschedule_requested`.
116	  """
117	  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
118	    Notification
119	    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
120	    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
121	    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
122	    |> limit(1)
123	    |> select([n], n.status)
124	    |> Repo.one()
125	  end
126	
127	  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook
128	
129	  @doc """
130	  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
131	  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
132	  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
133	  """
134	  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
135	      when is_binary(sid) do
136	    # Most-recent match: real SIDs are unique, but webhook retries racing
137	    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.
138	    notification =
139	      from(n in Notification,
140	        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,
141	        order_by: [desc: n.inserted_at],
142	        limit: 1
143	      )
144	      |> Repo.one()
145	
146	    case notification do
147	      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
148	      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
149	    end
150	  end
151	
152	  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}
153	
154	  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
155	    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
156	  end
157	
158	  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
159	       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
160	    with {:ok, updated} <-
161	           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
162	      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
163	      {:ok, updated}
164	    end
165	  end
166	
167	  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}
168	
169	  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
170	         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
171	       )
172	       when not is_nil(client_id) do
173	    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
174	    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
175	    token = generate_token()
176	
177	    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
178	    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")
179	
180	    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)
181	
182	    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
183	    |> Notification.changeset(%{
184	      client_id: client.id,
185	      job_id: job.id,
186	      kind: :reminder,
187	      channel: :email,
188	      status: :sent,
189	      token: token,
190	      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
191	    })
192	    |> Repo.insert()
193	  end
194	
195	  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok
196	
197	  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)
198	
199	  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
200	    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
201	      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
202	    else
203	      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
204	    end
205	  end
206	
207	  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
208	  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
209	    Notification
210	    |> where(
211	      [n],
212	      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
213	    )
214	    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
215	    |> Repo.all()
216	  end
217	
218	  @doc """
219	  Job ids whose most recent schedule-change notification hasn't been
220	  acknowledged (`:pending` or `:escalated`) — for `ScheduleLive.Index`
221	  to keep a cancelled job's row (and its ack-status/channel
222	  indicators) on the board until the office has visibility into it,
223	  per story 843's escalation path. A job with no schedule-change
224	  notification at all, or whose latest one is already `:acknowledged`,
225	  is left out.
226	  """
227	  def job_ids_with_unacknowledged_schedule_change(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
228	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
229	    Notification
230	    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change)
231	    |> distinct([n], n.job_id)
232	    |> order_by([n], asc: n.job_id, desc: n.inserted_at)
233	    |> select([n], {n.job_id, n.status})
234	    |> Repo.all()
235	    |> Enum.filter(fn {_job_id, status} -> status != :acknowledged end)
236	    |> Enum.map(fn {job_id, _status} -> job_id end)
237	  end
238	
239	  @doc """
240	  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
241	  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
242	  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
243	  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
244	  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
245	  ack status on the board.
246	  """
247	  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
248	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
249	    Notification
250	    |> where(
251	      [n],
252	      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
253	    )
254	    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
255	    |> limit(1)
256	    |> Repo.one()
257	    |> maybe_escalate()
258	  end
259	
260	  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
261	  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
262	  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
263	  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
264	  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
265	  # stale "pending" past the window.
266	  @escalation_window_seconds 600
267	
268	  defp maybe_escalate(%Notification{status: :pending} = notification) do
269	    if escalation_due?(notification) do
270	      {:ok, updated} =
271	        update_status(notification,
272	          status: :escalated,
273	          channel: :sms,
274	          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
275	        )
276	
277	      updated
278	    else
279	      notification
280	    end
281	  end
282	
283	  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification
284	
285	  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false
286	
287	  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do
288	    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, job_id)
289	
290	    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
291	      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
292	  end
293	
294	  ## Shared helpers
295	
296	  @doc false
297	  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)
298	
299	  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
300	    notification
301	    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
302	    |> Repo.update()
303	  end
304	
305	  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
306	  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
307	  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
308	  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
309	end

  @moduledoc """
  Client appointment reminders with confirm/reschedule actions, and
  cleaner schedule-change alerts requiring explicit acknowledgment with
  office visibility into what's still unacknowledged. Email/SMS
  delivery is abstracted behind `CleanerCrm.Notifications.Delivery`.

  Most functions are scoped by the caller's `Scope`. The confirm,
  reschedule, and delivery-status webhook endpoints are reached by an
  unauthenticated client or provider, so they look a notification up by
  its opaque `token` (or the provider's message id) instead.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{
    Notification,
    ReminderNotifier,
    ReminderScheduler,
    ReminderSettings
  }

  ## Reminder settings

  @doc "The account's reminder settings, defaulting to a 24-hour lead time if never configured."
  def get_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(ReminderSettings, account_id: account_id) do
      nil -> %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id}
      settings -> settings
    end
  end

  def change_reminder_settings(%Scope{} = scope, attrs \\ %{}) do
    scope |> get_reminder_settings() |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
  end

  def update_reminder_settings(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_reminder_settings()
    |> ReminderSettings.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end

  @doc "Runs the periodic reminder scan now — see `CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler`."
  defdelegate send_due_reminders(), to: ReminderScheduler, as: :scan_and_send

  ## Notifications

  def create_notification(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Notification{account_id: account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc "The office's delivery log: every notification for the account, most recent first."
  def list_notifications(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> preload([:client, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Public confirm/reschedule — reached by token, no scope available

  def get_notification_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Repo.get_by(Notification, token: token)
  end

  def confirm_reminder(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :confirmed, confirmed_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  def request_reschedule(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification,
        status: :reschedule_requested,
        reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.utc_now()
      )
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "True once the client has confirmed the most recent reminder sent for this job."
  def job_confirmed?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :confirmed)
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc "True once the client has asked to reschedule via the most recent reminder for this job."
  def reschedule_requested?(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder and n.status == :reschedule_requested
    )
    |> Repo.exists?()
  end

  @doc """
  The client's confirm/reschedule decision on their most recent
  reminder for this job, for `ScheduleLive.Index` to render on the
  board — `nil` (no decision yet), `:confirmed`, or
  `:reschedule_requested`.
  """
  def reminder_status_for_job(job_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :reminder)
    |> where([n], n.status in [:confirmed, :reschedule_requested])
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> select([n], n.status)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  ## Twilio delivery-status webhook

  @doc """
  Applies a Twilio status callback: marks the matching notification
  delivered or undelivered, and — for an undeliverable SMS reminder —
  falls back to emailing the client and flags it for office visibility.
  """
  def handle_delivery_status(%{"MessageSid" => sid, "MessageStatus" => status} = params)
      when is_binary(sid) do
    # Most-recent match: real SIDs are unique, but webhook retries racing
    # inserts (or duplicated test data) must not 500 the endpoint.
    notification =
      from(n in Notification,
        where: n.provider_message_id == ^sid,
        order_by: [desc: n.inserted_at],
        limit: 1
      )
      |> Repo.one()

    case notification do
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
      notification -> apply_delivery_status(notification, status, params["ErrorCode"])
    end
  end

  def handle_delivery_status(_params), do: {:error, :invalid_payload}

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, "delivered", _error_code) do
    update_status(notification, status: :delivered, delivered_at: DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, status, error_code)
       when status in ["failed", "undelivered"] do
    with {:ok, updated} <-
           update_status(notification, status: :undelivered, failure_reason: error_code || status) do
      maybe_fallback_to_email(updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  defp apply_delivery_status(notification, _status, _error_code), do: {:ok, notification}

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(
         %Notification{kind: :reminder, channel: :sms, client_id: client_id} = notification
       )
       when not is_nil(client_id) do
    client = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, notification.client_id)
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, notification.job_id)
    token = generate_token()

    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    %Notification{account_id: notification.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: :email,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      sent_at: DateTime.utc_now()
    })
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp maybe_fallback_to_email(_notification), do: :ok

  ## Schedule-change alerts (story 843 groundwork)

  def acknowledge(token) when is_binary(token) do
    with %Notification{} = notification <- get_notification_by_token(token) do
      update_status(notification, status: :acknowledged, acknowledged_at: DateTime.utc_now())
    else
      nil -> {:error, :not_found}
    end
  end

  @doc "Pending schedule-change alerts a cleaner hasn't acknowledged yet, for office visibility."
  def list_unacknowledged(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change and n.status == :pending
    )
    |> preload([:cleaner, :job])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Job ids whose most recent schedule-change notification hasn't been
  acknowledged (`:pending` or `:escalated`) — for `ScheduleLive.Index`
  to keep a cancelled job's row (and its ack-status/channel
  indicators) on the board until the office has visibility into it,
  per story 843's escalation path. A job with no schedule-change
  notification at all, or whose latest one is already `:acknowledged`,
  is left out.
  """
  def job_ids_with_unacknowledged_schedule_change(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id})
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where([n], n.account_id == ^account_id and n.kind == :schedule_change)
    |> distinct([n], n.job_id)
    |> order_by([n], asc: n.job_id, desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> select([n], {n.job_id, n.status})
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.filter(fn {_job_id, status} -> status != :acknowledged end)
    |> Enum.map(fn {job_id, _status} -> job_id end)
  end

  @doc """
  The most recent schedule-change alert pushed for this job — `nil`,
  or a `Notification` exposing `:status`
  (`:pending` | `:acknowledged` | `:escalated`) and `:channel`
  (`:push` | `:sms` | `:email`). This is the contract
  `CleanerCrmWeb.ScheduleLive.Index` reads defensively to show a job's
  ack status on the board.
  """
  def latest_schedule_change_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, job_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Notification
    |> where(
      [n],
      n.account_id == ^account_id and n.job_id == ^job_id and n.kind == :schedule_change
    )
    |> order_by([n], desc: n.inserted_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
    |> maybe_escalate()
  end

  # A same-day change nobody has acknowledged within the escalation
  # window re-sends via the fallback channel (SMS) and flags as
  # escalated for office visibility. Computed on read rather than a
  # separate periodic pass — every read of a job's alert (the board,
  # `FieldLive.Today`) goes through here, so none of them can show a
  # stale "pending" past the window.
  @escalation_window_seconds 600

  defp maybe_escalate(%Notification{status: :pending} = notification) do
    if escalation_due?(notification) do
      {:ok, updated} =
        update_status(notification,
          status: :escalated,
          channel: :sms,
          escalated_at: DateTime.utc_now()
        )

      updated
    else
      notification
    end
  end

  defp maybe_escalate(notification), do: notification

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: nil}), do: false

  defp escalation_due?(%Notification{pushed_at: pushed_at, job_id: job_id}) do
    job = Repo.get!(CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, job_id)

    Date.compare(job.scheduled_date, Date.utc_today()) != :gt and
      DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), pushed_at, :second) >= @escalation_window_seconds
  end

  ## Shared helpers

  @doc false
  def generate_token, do: Base.url_encode64(:crypto.strong_rand_bytes(24), padding: false)

  defp update_status(%Notification{} = notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> Notification.changeset(Map.new(attrs))
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story837.Criterion7183Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 837 — Send automated appointment reminders to clients
  Criterion 7183 — Reminder fires at the configured lead time

  The scheduler's automatic trigger has no user-facing action to
  drive — the spec cannot call `CleanerCrm.Notifications` directly
  (sealed boundary). The appointment is pinned to the exact
  lead-time boundary (24 hours from now) so any conforming
  implementation's periodic check has already fired the send by the
  time `then_` asserts; `when_` marks that moment rather than
  performing an action. This is the one spec that proves the
  automatic trigger end-to-end — criteria 7185–7189 seed an
  already-sent reminder instead of re-driving it.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "an appointment reminder fires automatically at the configured lead time" do
    scenario "reminder fires at the configured lead time" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the owner's reminder lead time is set to 24 hours", context do
        {:ok, reminders_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/reminders")

        reminders_live
        |> form("[data-test='reminder-settings-form']", settings: %{lead_time_hours: "24"})
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      given_ "a client has an appointment 24 hours from now", context do
        client =
          Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{
            email: "jamie-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com",
            preferred_channel: :email
          })

        due_at = lead_time_boundary()

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            scheduled_date: DateTime.to_date(due_at),
            start_time: DateTime.to_time(due_at)
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the clock reaches the configured lead time before the appointment", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "an appointment reminder is automatically sent to the client", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end

  defp lead_time_boundary, do: DateTime.add(DateTime.utc_now(), 24 * 60 * 60, :second)
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Schedules reminder sends ahead of upcoming jobs.
4	
5	  Driven by Oban's cron plugin in production (see the
6	  background-jobs-oban ADR): `perform/1` runs on a schedule and calls
7	  `scan_and_send/1`, the pure entry point, so the same check can also
8	  be run synchronously — deterministic, no clock-waiting — right after
9	  a job is created.
10	
11	  Only accounts that have explicitly saved reminder settings
12	  (`CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive`) are scanned, so this never fires for
13	  an account that hasn't opted in.
14	  """
15	
16	  use Oban.Worker, queue: :notifications
17	
18	  import Ecto.Query
19	  require Logger
20	
21	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
22	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
23	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Delivery, Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderSettings}
25	
26	  @impl Oban.Worker
27	  def perform(%Oban.Job{}) do
28	    scan_and_send()
29	    :ok
30	  end
31	
32	  @doc "Sends every reminder that's due right now, across every account with reminder settings."
33	  def scan_and_send(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
34	    ReminderSettings
35	    |> Repo.all()
36	    |> Enum.each(&send_for_account(&1, now))
37	  end
38	
39	  defp send_for_account(
40	         %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id, lead_time_hours: lead_time_hours},
41	         now
42	       ) do
43	    account_id
44	    |> due_jobs()
45	    |> Enum.filter(&due_now?(&1, lead_time_hours, now))
46	    |> Enum.each(&send_reminder_isolated/1)
47	  end
48	
49	  # One job's send failing (a delivery-adapter bug, a bad email
50	  # address, whatever) must never stop the rest of the scan — each job
51	  # gets its own failure boundary rather than the whole `Enum.each`
52	  # aborting on the first raise.
53	  defp send_reminder_isolated(job) do
54	    send_reminder(job)
55	  rescue
56	    error ->
57	      Logger.error(
58	        "ReminderScheduler failed to send reminder for job #{job.id}: " <>
59	          Exception.format(:error, error, __STACKTRACE__)
60	      )
61	  end
62	
63	  defp due_jobs(account_id) do
64	    already_reminded =
65	      from n in Notification, where: n.job_id == parent_as(:job).id and n.kind == :reminder
66	
67	    from(j in Job,
68	      as: :job,
69	      where: j.account_id == ^account_id,
70	      where: j.status == :scheduled,
71	      where: not is_nil(j.client_id),
72	      where: not exists(already_reminded),
73	      preload: [:client]
74	    )
75	    |> Repo.all()
76	  end
77	
78	  defp due_now?(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}, lead_time_hours, now) do
79	    with {:ok, start_at} <- DateTime.new(date, time, "Etc/UTC") do
80	      due_at = DateTime.add(start_at, -lead_time_hours * 3600, :second)
81	      DateTime.compare(due_at, now) != :gt and DateTime.compare(start_at, now) == :gt
82	    else
83	      _ -> false
84	    end
85	  end
86	
87	  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: %Client{preferred_channel: :sms, phone: phone}} = job)
88	       when is_binary(phone) do
89	    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
90	    body = reminder_sms_body(job, token)
91	
92	    case Delivery.send_sms(phone, body) do
93	      {:ok, %{provider_message_id: sid}} ->
94	        insert_notification!(job, job.client, :sms, token, sid, DateTime.utc_now())
95	
96	      {:error, _reason} ->
97	        send_email_reminder(job, job.client)
98	    end
99	  end
100	
101	  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: client} = job), do: send_email_reminder(job, client)
102	
103	  defp send_email_reminder(job, client) do
104	    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
105	    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
106	    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")
107	
108	    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)
109	
110	    insert_notification!(job, client, :email, token, nil, DateTime.utc_now())
111	  end
112	
113	  defp reminder_sms_body(job, token) do
114	    "Cleaning appointment reminder for #{job.scheduled_date} at #{job.start_time}. " <>
115	      "Confirm: #{reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")} " <>
116	      "Reschedule: #{reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")}"
117	  end
118	
119	  defp insert_notification!(job, client, channel, token, provider_message_id, sent_at) do
120	    %Notification{account_id: job.account_id}
121	    |> Notification.changeset(%{
122	      client_id: client.id,
123	      job_id: job.id,
124	      kind: :reminder,
125	      channel: channel,
126	      status: :sent,
127	      token: token,
128	      provider_message_id: provider_message_id,
129	      sent_at: sent_at
130	    })
131	    |> Repo.insert!()
132	  end
133	
134	  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
135	  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.ReminderScheduler do
  @moduledoc """
  Schedules reminder sends ahead of upcoming jobs.

  Driven by Oban's cron plugin in production (see the
  background-jobs-oban ADR): `perform/1` runs on a schedule and calls
  `scan_and_send/1`, the pure entry point, so the same check can also
  be run synchronously — deterministic, no clock-waiting — right after
  a job is created.

  Only accounts that have explicitly saved reminder settings
  (`CleanerCrmWeb.ReminderLive`) are scanned, so this never fires for
  an account that hasn't opted in.
  """

  use Oban.Worker, queue: :notifications

  import Ecto.Query
  require Logger

  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Notifications.{Delivery, Notification, ReminderNotifier, ReminderSettings}

  @impl Oban.Worker
  def perform(%Oban.Job{}) do
    scan_and_send()
    :ok
  end

  @doc "Sends every reminder that's due right now, across every account with reminder settings."
  def scan_and_send(now \\ DateTime.utc_now()) do
    ReminderSettings
    |> Repo.all()
    |> Enum.each(&send_for_account(&1, now))
  end

  defp send_for_account(
         %ReminderSettings{account_id: account_id, lead_time_hours: lead_time_hours},
         now
       ) do
    account_id
    |> due_jobs()
    |> Enum.filter(&due_now?(&1, lead_time_hours, now))
    |> Enum.each(&send_reminder_isolated/1)
  end

  # One job's send failing (a delivery-adapter bug, a bad email
  # address, whatever) must never stop the rest of the scan — each job
  # gets its own failure boundary rather than the whole `Enum.each`
  # aborting on the first raise.
  defp send_reminder_isolated(job) do
    send_reminder(job)
  rescue
    error ->
      Logger.error(
        "ReminderScheduler failed to send reminder for job #{job.id}: " <>
          Exception.format(:error, error, __STACKTRACE__)
      )
  end

  defp due_jobs(account_id) do
    already_reminded =
      from n in Notification, where: n.job_id == parent_as(:job).id and n.kind == :reminder

    from(j in Job,
      as: :job,
      where: j.account_id == ^account_id,
      where: j.status == :scheduled,
      where: not is_nil(j.client_id),
      where: not exists(already_reminded),
      preload: [:client]
    )
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp due_now?(%Job{scheduled_date: date, start_time: time}, lead_time_hours, now) do
    with {:ok, start_at} <- DateTime.new(date, time, "Etc/UTC") do
      due_at = DateTime.add(start_at, -lead_time_hours * 3600, :second)
      DateTime.compare(due_at, now) != :gt and DateTime.compare(start_at, now) == :gt
    else
      _ -> false
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: %Client{preferred_channel: :sms, phone: phone}} = job)
       when is_binary(phone) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    body = reminder_sms_body(job, token)

    case Delivery.send_sms(phone, body) do
      {:ok, %{provider_message_id: sid}} ->
        insert_notification!(job, job.client, :sms, token, sid, DateTime.utc_now())

      {:error, _reason} ->
        send_email_reminder(job, job.client)
    end
  end

  defp send_reminder(%Job{client: client} = job), do: send_email_reminder(job, client)

  defp send_email_reminder(job, client) do
    token = CleanerCrm.Notifications.generate_token()
    confirm_url = reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")
    reschedule_url = reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")

    {:ok, _email} = ReminderNotifier.deliver_reminder(client, job, confirm_url, reschedule_url)

    insert_notification!(job, client, :email, token, nil, DateTime.utc_now())
  end

  defp reminder_sms_body(job, token) do
    "Cleaning appointment reminder for #{job.scheduled_date} at #{job.start_time}. " <>
      "Confirm: #{reminder_url("/reminders/confirm/#{token}")} " <>
      "Reschedule: #{reminder_url("/reminders/reschedule/#{token}")}"
  end

  defp insert_notification!(job, client, channel, token, provider_message_id, sent_at) do
    %Notification{account_id: job.account_id}
    |> Notification.changeset(%{
      client_id: client.id,
      job_id: job.id,
      kind: :reminder,
      channel: channel,
      status: :sent,
      token: token,
      provider_message_id: provider_message_id,
      sent_at: sent_at
    })
    |> Repo.insert!()
  end

  # `CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url()` is the standard phx.gen.auth-style
  # exception for building absolute links in outbound messages — see
  # the `dirty_xrefs` note on the `CleanerCrm` boundary.
  defp reminder_url(path), do: CleanerCrmWeb.Endpoint.url() <> path
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job do
  @moduledoc """
  A single scheduled visit: a property (or client), a time window, and
  an optional assigned cleaner.

  A job is either a one-off (`recurring_plan_id` is `nil`) or one
  occurrence materialized from a `RecurringPlan`'s cadence (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence`). Both `client_id` and
  `property_id` are independently optional at the schema level — some
  callers (time tracking, quality, notifications) only ever have a
  client on hand, while the schedule board's own job form always
  carries a property.

  ## Status

  `:scheduled` (default) -> `:in_progress` -> `:completed`, or
  `:scheduled` -> `:cancelled`. Transitions beyond create/cancel belong
  to other contexts (time tracking clocks a job into `:in_progress`).

  ## Pay fields

  `pay_type`/`hourly_rate_cents`/`piece_rate_cents` describe what the
  *cleaner* earns for this job — as distinct from `agreed_price_cents`,
  what the *client* is charged. They live here rather than on a
  separate table for the same reason `agreed_price_cents` does: a
  job's pay arrangement is a one-off property of that job, read and
  written by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` rather than by Scheduling
  itself.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          property_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          recurring_plan_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          scheduled_date: Date.t() | nil,
          start_time: Time.t() | nil,
          end_time: Time.t() | nil,
          status: :scheduled | :in_progress | :completed | :cancelled,
          agreed_price_cents: integer() | nil,
          pay_type: :hourly | :piece_rate | nil,
          hourly_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          piece_rate_cents: integer() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "jobs" do
    field :scheduled_date, :date
    field :start_time, :time
    field :end_time, :time

    field :status, Ecto.Enum,
      values: [:scheduled, :in_progress, :completed, :cancelled],
      default: :scheduled

    field :agreed_price_cents, :integer
    field :agreed_price, :decimal, virtual: true

    field :pay_type, Ecto.Enum, values: [:hourly, :piece_rate]
    field :hourly_rate_cents, :integer
    field :piece_rate_cents, :integer

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :property, CleanerCrm.Clients.Property, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :recurring_plan, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id property_id cleaner_id recurring_plan_id scheduled_date
             start_time end_time status agreed_price_cents agreed_price
             pay_type hourly_rate_cents piece_rate_cents)a

  def changeset(job, attrs) do
    job
    |> cast(rename_date_key(attrs), @fields)
    |> validate_required([:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])
    |> validate_time_order()
    |> put_agreed_price_cents()
  end

  # The board's own job form asks for a plain "date" — friendlier than
  # "scheduled date" — while some spex drive the same form with a
  # `scheduled_date` override instead (matching the schema field name
  # directly). The form carries a second, always-blank
  # `job[scheduled_date]` field purely as a landing pad for that
  # override key (`Phoenix.LiveViewTest.form/3` requires an override's
  # key to match a real field name in the form). Whichever one arrives
  # non-blank wins; `scheduled_date` takes precedence when both do,
  # since a still-blank landing pad means only `date` was ever touched.
  defp rename_date_key(%{"scheduled_date" => sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, "date")

  defp rename_date_key(%{scheduled_date: sd} = attrs) when sd not in [nil, ""],
    do: Map.delete(attrs, :date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{"date" => date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete("date") |> Map.put("scheduled_date", date)

  defp rename_date_key(%{date: date} = attrs),
    do: attrs |> Map.delete(:date) |> Map.put(:scheduled_date, date)

  defp rename_date_key(attrs), do: attrs

  defp validate_time_order(changeset) do
    start_time = get_field(changeset, :start_time)
    end_time = get_field(changeset, :end_time)

    if start_time && end_time && Time.compare(start_time, end_time) != :lt do
      add_error(changeset, :end_time, "must be after the start time")
    else
      changeset
    end
  end

  # `agreed_price` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the
  # money-handling ADR's rate math); it is rounded half-up and stored
  # as `agreed_price_cents` — the only column ever persisted.
  defp put_agreed_price_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :agreed_price) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :agreed_price_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end
