1	defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
4	  conflict-aware assignment.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
7	  """
8	
9	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
10	
11	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
12	  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
15	
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
17	    AvailabilityBlock,
18	    ConflictDetector,
19	    Job,
20	    Recurrence,
21	    RecurringPlan
22	  }
23	
24	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
25	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User
26	
27	  ## Jobs
28	
29	  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    Job
31	    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
32	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
33	    |> Repo.get!(id)
34	  end
35	
36	  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
37	    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
38	  end
39	
40	  @doc """
41	  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
42	  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
43	  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
44	  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
45	  """
46	  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
47	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
48	    with {:ok, job} <-
49	           %Job{account_id: account_id}
50	           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
51	           |> Repo.insert() do
52	      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
53	      {:ok, job}
54	    end
55	  end
56	
57	  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
58	  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
59	  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
60	  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
61	  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
62	  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
63	  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
64	  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
65	  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
66	  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
67	  # left alone.
68	  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
69	    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
70	      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
71	        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
72	        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
73	      end
74	    else
75	      attrs
76	    end
77	  end
78	
79	  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
80	    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
81	      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
82	        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
83	        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
84	        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
85	          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
86	        else
87	          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
88	        end
89	
90	      _ ->
91	        attrs
92	    end
93	  end
94	
95	  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))
96	
97	  defp blank?(nil), do: true
98	  defp blank?(""), do: true
99	  defp blank?(_value), do: false
100	
101	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
102	    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
103	  end
104	
105	  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
106	    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
107	  end
108	
109	  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
110	  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
111	  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
112	  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
113	  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
114	  defp job_created_values(job) do
115	    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
116	  end
117	
118	  @doc """
119	  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
120	  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
121	  """
122	  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
123	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
124	    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)
125	
126	    Job
127	    |> where(
128	      [j],
129	      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
130	        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
131	    )
132	    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
133	    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
134	    |> Repo.all()
135	  end
136	
137	  @doc """
138	  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
139	  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
140	  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
141	  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.
142	
143	  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
144	  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
145	  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
146	  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
147	  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
148	  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
149	  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
150	  """
151	  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
152	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
153	    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])

defmodule CleanerCrm.Scheduling do
  @moduledoc """
  Recurring plans and the jobs they generate, cleaner time-off, and
  conflict-aware assignment.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Audit.Recorder
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Property
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.{
    AvailabilityBlock,
    ConflictDetector,
    Job,
    Recurrence,
    RecurringPlan
  }

  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.User

  ## Jobs

  def get_job!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Job
    |> where([j], j.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_job(%Scope{}, %Job{} = job, attrs \\ %{}) do
    Job.changeset(job, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a job. Recorded in the audit trail as authored by the
  caller, unless `actor: :system` is passed — used when the job is one
  occurrence materialized from a recurring plan rather than a job a
  human directly asked for (see `create_recurring_plan/2`).
  """
  def create_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, job} <-
           %Job{account_id: account_id}
           |> Job.changeset(derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))
           |> Repo.insert() do
      record_job_created(scope, job, Keyword.get(opts, :actor, :user))
      {:ok, job}
    end
  end

  # The board's own job form (and a recurring plan's own materialized
  # occurrences, via `Recurrence.job_attrs/1`) only ever carry a
  # `property_id` — never a `client_id` — so a job created either way
  # otherwise saves with `client_id: nil`. That breaks anything reading
  # the client straight off the job rather than through its property
  # (story 836's invoicing does both a card-on-file charge lookup and
  # the invoice's own client label this way), so every job creation
  # backfills `client_id` from its property here rather than requiring
  # every caller to remember to. A caller that already supplies a
  # `client_id` (fixtures with only a client on hand, no property) is
  # left alone.
  defp derive_client_id(account_id, attrs) do
    if blank?(fetch_attr(attrs, :client_id)) do
      case fetch_attr(attrs, :property_id) do
        value when value in [nil, ""] -> attrs
        property_id -> put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id)
      end
    else
      attrs
    end
  end

  defp put_client_id_from_property(attrs, account_id, property_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Property, id: property_id, account_id: account_id) do
      %Property{client_id: client_id} when not is_nil(client_id) ->
        # Match whichever key style (atom or string) `attrs` already
        # uses — `Ecto.Changeset.cast/4` raises on a map mixing both.
        if Map.has_key?(attrs, :property_id) do
          Map.put(attrs, :client_id, client_id)
        else
          Map.put(attrs, "client_id", client_id)
        end

      _ ->
        attrs
    end
  end

  defp fetch_attr(attrs, key), do: Map.get(attrs, key) || Map.get(attrs, to_string(key))

  defp blank?(nil), do: true
  defp blank?(""), do: true
  defp blank?(_value), do: false

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :system) do
    Recorder.record_system(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  defp record_job_created(scope, job, :user) do
    Recorder.record(scope, "job_created", "Job", job.id, %{}, job_created_values(job))
  end

  # Deliberately omits `scheduled_date`: a "created" entry's own
  # subject label (job → property/client) is enough to identify which
  # job this is, and surfacing it here would read as a schedule change
  # (`field_changes/1`'s "Scheduled date: ..." line) indistinguishable
  # from an actual reschedule recorded later by `update_job/3`.
  defp job_created_values(job) do
    %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id}
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every job scheduled between `week_start` and six days later,
  cleaner/property/client preloaded, ordered for the board.
  """
  def list_jobs_for_week(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Date{} = week_start)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    week_end = Date.add(week_start, 6)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.scheduled_date >= ^week_start and
        j.scheduled_date <= ^week_end and j.status != :cancelled
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists every non-cancelled job for the account, cleaner/property/client
  preloaded, ordered for the board. Unlike `list_jobs_for_week/2`, this
  isn't bounded to a single week — a recurring plan's series can span
  months, and the board needs to account for all of it at a glance.

  `:include_cancelled_ids` (default `[]`) admits specific cancelled
  jobs back in anyway — the board's own escape hatch for a cancelled
  job that still carries an unacknowledged schedule-change
  notification (story 843): the office needs to keep seeing its
  ack-status until the cleaner acknowledges, and the escalation check
  needs the job rendered at all to ever run. Other callers passing no
  opts see the same non-cancelled set as before.
  """
  def list_jobs(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, opts \\ [])
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    include_cancelled_ids = Keyword.get(opts, :include_cancelled_ids, [])

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and
        (j.status != :cancelled or j.id in ^include_cancelled_ids)
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:cleaner, :property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Assigns (or reassigns) a job to a cleaner, rejecting the move with
  `{:error, :unavailable}` or `{:error, :overlap}` when it conflicts
  with that cleaner's time off or an existing booking. A `nil`
  `cleaner_id` always succeeds (unassigning never conflicts).
  """
  def assign_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <-
           ConflictDetector.check_assignment(
             scope,
             cleaner_id,
             job.scheduled_date,
             job.start_time,
             job.end_time,
             exclude_job_id: job.id
           ),
         {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_reassigned",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"cleaner_id" => job.cleaner_id},
        %{"cleaner_id" => cleaner_id}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  def cancel_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_cancelled",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Updates a job's schedule and/or price — a reschedule, a price
  change, or both, made directly from the board rather than through
  `assign_cleaner/3`'s conflict-checked path. Records only the fields
  that actually changed to the audit trail, attributed to the caller.
  """
  def update_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    changeset = Job.changeset(job, derive_client_id(account_id, attrs))

    with {:ok, updated} <- Repo.update(changeset) do
      record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated)
      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  @audited_update_fields ~w(scheduled_date start_time end_time agreed_price_cents status)a

  defp record_job_updated(scope, job, changeset, updated) do
    changed_fields =
      changeset.changes
      |> Map.keys()
      |> Enum.filter(&(&1 in @audited_update_fields))

    if changed_fields != [] do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        update_action(changed_fields),
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        audit_snapshot(job, changed_fields),
        audit_snapshot(updated, changed_fields)
      )
    end
  end

  defp update_action(changed_fields) do
    cond do
      Enum.any?(changed_fields, &(&1 in [:scheduled_date, :start_time, :end_time])) ->
        "job_rescheduled"

      :agreed_price_cents in changed_fields ->
        "job_price_changed"

      true ->
        "job_updated"
    end
  end

  defp audit_snapshot(job, fields),
    do: Map.new(fields, &{to_string(&1), audit_value(Map.get(job, &1))})

  defp audit_value(%Date{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(%Time{} = value), do: to_string(value)
  defp audit_value(value), do: value

  @doc """
  Removes a job from the board without hard-deleting its row — the
  row (and any audit entries already about it) stays resolvable for
  the trail. Distinct from `cancel_job/2`: this is the office
  correcting a mistaken entry rather than calling off an appointment,
  so it's recorded as "deleted" rather than "cancelled" and never
  notifies the assigned cleaner.
  """
  def delete_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, updated} <- job |> Job.changeset(%{status: :cancelled}) |> Repo.update() do
      Recorder.record(
        scope,
        "job_deleted",
        "Job",
        updated.id,
        %{"status" => to_string(job.status)},
        %{"status" => "cancelled"}
      )

      {:ok, updated}
    end
  end

  ## Recurring plans

  def get_recurring_plan!(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    RecurringPlan
    |> where([p], p.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload([:property, :cleaner])
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  def change_recurring_plan(%Scope{}, %RecurringPlan{} = plan, attrs \\ %{}) do
    RecurringPlan.preview_changeset(plan, attrs)
  end

  @doc """
  Runs conflict detection for a (possibly unsaved) plan's full series
  against its preferred cleaner, without persisting anything. Returns
  only the conflicting occurrences, as `[%{index:, date:, reason:}]`.
  """
  def preview_conflicts(scope, %RecurringPlan{} = plan) do
    ConflictDetector.check_occurrences(scope, plan, Recurrence.occurrences(plan))
  end

  @doc """
  Saves a recurring plan and materializes its full series of jobs.
  Conflicting occurrences are still created and still assigned to the
  preferred cleaner — conflicts are for the owner to review and
  resolve, never a silent block on saving.
  """
  def create_recurring_plan(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, plan} <-
             %RecurringPlan{account_id: account_id}
             |> RecurringPlan.changeset(attrs)
             |> Repo.insert() do
        jobs =
          plan
          |> Recurrence.job_attrs()
          |> Enum.map(fn job_attrs ->
            {:ok, job} = create_job(scope, job_attrs, actor: :system)
            job
          end)

        {:ok, {plan, jobs}}
      end
    end)
  end

  ## Availability blocks

  def change_availability_block(%Scope{}, %AvailabilityBlock{} = block, attrs \\ %{}) do
    AvailabilityBlock.changeset(block, attrs)
  end

  def create_availability_block(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %AvailabilityBlock{account_id: account_id}
    |> AvailabilityBlock.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Cleaners (account members who take jobs)

  @doc """
  Lists the account's members as candidate cleaners for the board and
  assignment pickers.
  """
  def list_cleaners(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> Accounts.list_account_members(account_id)
    |> Enum.map(& &1.user)
  end

  @doc """
  Registers a new cleaner: a user identified by display name (rather
  than login credentials) added to the account as a member, so jobs
  and availability can be assigned to them. There is no login flow for
  a cleaner created this way — see `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.cleaner_fixture/3`
  for the (real, login-capable) path other stories seed cleaners
  through.
  """
  def register_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, name)
      when not is_nil(account_id) and is_binary(name) do
    with {:ok, user} <- insert_cleaner_user(name),
         {:ok, _member} <- Accounts.add_user_to_account(scope, user.id, account_id, :member) do
      {:ok, user}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Fetches a single cleaner by id, for their detail page. Draws from
  the same membership list as `list_cleaners/1`, so a user who isn't
  a member of this account can't be looked up here either. Raises if
  not found.
  """
  def get_cleaner!(%Scope{} = scope, id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(id)

    scope
    |> list_cleaners()
    |> Enum.find(&(&1.id == cleaner_id))
    |> case do
      nil -> raise Ecto.NoResultsError, queryable: User
      cleaner -> cleaner
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's time-off blocks for their detail page, soonest
  first.
  """
  def list_availability_blocks(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    AvailabilityBlock
    |> where([b], b.account_id == ^account_id and b.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id)
    |> order_by([b], asc: b.date)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  @doc """
  Lists a cleaner's upcoming (today or later, non-cancelled) jobs for
  their detail page, soonest first.
  """
  def list_upcoming_jobs_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    cleaner_id = parse_cleaner_id(cleaner_id)

    Job
    |> where(
      [j],
      j.account_id == ^account_id and j.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and
        j.status != :cancelled and j.scheduled_date >= ^Date.utc_today()
    )
    |> order_by([j], asc: j.scheduled_date, asc: j.start_time)
    |> preload([:property, :client])
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_integer(id), do: id
  defp parse_cleaner_id(id) when is_binary(id), do: String.to_integer(id)

  defp insert_cleaner_user(name) do
    %User{}
    |> Ecto.Changeset.cast(%{name: name, email: placeholder_email(name)}, [:name, :email])
    |> Ecto.Changeset.validate_required([:name, :email])
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  defp placeholder_email(name) do
    slug =
      name
      |> String.downcase()
      |> String.replace(~r/[^a-z0-9]+/, ".")
      |> String.trim(".")

    "#{slug}-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@cleaners.local"
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing do
  @moduledoc """
  Invoices generated from completed jobs and payment collection via
  card-on-file or a public payment link, with proof-of-work attached
  from `CleanerCrm.Quality` for chargeback defense.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, an invoice's `status` only ever advances
  on a Stripe webhook confirmation: `charge_card/2` and
  `pay_via_link/2` just submit a PaymentIntent and move the invoice to
  `:charge_pending`; only `receive_webhook/1` marks it `:paid`, or
  reverts it to `:unpaid` on a decline so the owner can retry or send a
  payment link.

  Every function that isn't reached from the public `/pay/:token` or
  `/webhooks/stripe` routes is scoped to the caller's active account —

  itself lives in `CleanerCrm.Quality.complete_job/2`

  yet either). Once it does, the natural hook is right there — call
  `generate_for_job/2` with the now-completed job after
  `Quality.complete_job/2` succeeds.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Billing.{Invoice, Payment, ReceiptNotifier, StripeGateway}
  alias CleanerCrm.Clients.Client
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.Scope

  ## Invoices

  @doc "Lists the account's invoices, most recent first, for the billing queue."
  def list_invoices(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> order_by([i], desc: i.inserted_at)
    |> preload(job: :client)

    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.get!(id)
  end

  @doc """
  Looks up an invoice by its public payment-link token. Takes no
  `Scope` — the payer on `/pay/:token` isn't a logged-in user, so the
  token itself (unguessable, unique) is the only access control this
  lookup has.
  """
  def get_invoice_by_token(token) when is_binary(token) do
    Invoice
    |> where([i], i.payment_token == ^token)
    |> preload(job: :client)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def create_invoice(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, attrs) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    %Invoice{account_id: account_id}
    |> Invoice.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Generates the invoice for a job that's just been marked complete —
  see the moduledoc for where this gets wired in once job completion
  has a real caller.

  Returns `{:error, :no_price}` without creating an invoice, and
  without touching the database at all, when the job has no
  `agreed_price_cents` — e.g. a visit materialized from a
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.RecurringPlan` with no price set (see
  `CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Recurrence.job_attrs/1`). Job completion itself
  must still succeed in that case, so callers should let this error
  through rather than fail the completion on it. There's no dedicated
  "completed jobs missing an invoice" queue today — the office notices
  a missing invoice by comparing the schedule board's completed jobs
  against `list_invoices/1`, or avoids it entirely by pricing the job
  (or its recurring plan) before it's completed.
  """
  def generate_for_job(%Scope{}, %Job{agreed_price_cents: nil}), do: {:error, :no_price}

  def generate_for_job(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    create_invoice(scope, %{job_id: job.id, amount_cents: job.agreed_price_cents, status: :unpaid})
  end

  ## Payment collection

  @doc """
  Charges the client's card on file for the invoice's full amount.
  Refused with `{:error, :no_card_on_file}` when the client has none.
  """
  def charge_card(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice

      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> invoice_client()
    |> submit_and_finalize_charge(invoice, off_session: true, source: "card_on_file")
  end

  defp submit_and_finalize_charge(%Client{} = client, invoice, opts) do
    {source, charge_opts} = Keyword.pop!(opts, :source)

    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <-
           submit_charge(invoice, payment_method_for(client), charge_opts) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, client, intent_id, source)
    end

  public payment-link token — the `/pay/:token` page's own flow, with
  no card on file and no logged-in payer to scope against.
  """
  def pay_via_link(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method) when is_binary(payment_method) do
    with {:ok, %{id: intent_id}} <- submit_charge(invoice, payment_method, off_session: false) do
      finalize_charge_submission(invoice, invoice_client(invoice), intent_id, "payment_link")
    end
  end

  defp submit_charge(%Invoice{} = invoice, payment_method, opts) do
    StripeGateway.create_payment_intent(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      payment_method: payment_method,
      off_session: Keyword.get(opts, :off_session, false),
      metadata: %{invoice_id: invoice.id}
    })

  # SetupIntent-backed token is stored. The Test adapter ignores it
  # entirely, and the Live adapter is never exercised without one.
  defp payment_method_for(%Client{id: id}), do: "card_on_file:#{id}"

  defp finalize_charge_submission(%Invoice{} = invoice, client, intent_id, source) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <-
             invoice
             |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: :charge_pending, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id})
             |> Repo.update(),
           {:ok, _payment} <- record_payment(updated, intent_id, source, :pending) do
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
    |> tap(fn
      {:ok, updated} -> send_receipt(client, updated)
      _error -> :ok
    end)
  end

  @doc """
  Generates (or reuses) an invoice's public payment-link token, so the
  owner can share `/pay/:token` with a client who has no card on file.
  """
  def create_payment_link(
        %Scope{active_account_id: account_id},
        %Invoice{account_id: account_id} = invoice
      )
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    invoice
    |> Invoice.changeset(%{payment_token: invoice.payment_token || generate_token()})
    |> Repo.update()
  end

  defp generate_token, do: 16 |> :crypto.strong_rand_bytes() |> Base.url_encode64(padding: false)

  defp invoice_client(%Invoice{} = invoice) do
    invoice |> Repo.preload(job: :client) |> then(& &1.job.client)
  end

  defp send_receipt(%Client{email: email}, %Invoice{} = invoice) when is_binary(email) do
    ReceiptNotifier.deliver_receipt(email, invoice)
    :ok
  end

  defp send_receipt(_client, _invoice), do: :ok

  defp record_payment(%Invoice{} = invoice, intent_id, source, status) do
    %Payment{account_id: invoice.account_id, invoice_id: invoice.id}
    |> Payment.changeset(%{
      amount_cents: invoice.amount_cents,
      status: status,
      provider: "stripe",
      stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id,
      source: source

    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  ## Webhook

  @doc """
  Verifies and applies an inbound Stripe webhook request — the
  controller's only touchpoint into this context, so it never sees
  event data it can't trust.
  """
  def receive_webhook(conn) do
    with {:ok, event} <- StripeGateway.verify_webhook_event(conn) do
      apply_webhook_event(event)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.succeeded"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :paid, :succeeded)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => "payment_intent.payment_failed"} = event) do
    with {:ok, invoice} <- find_invoice_for_event(event) do
      transition_invoice(invoice, :unpaid, :failed)
    end
  end

  defp apply_webhook_event(%{"type" => _other}), do: {:ok, :ignored}

  defp find_invoice_for_event(%{"data" => %{"object" => object}}) do
    case object do
      %{"metadata" => %{"invoice_id" => invoice_id}} when is_binary(invoice_id) ->
        fetch_invoice(invoice_id)

      %{"id" => intent_id} when is_binary(intent_id) ->
        fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id)

      _ ->
        {:error, :invoice_not_found}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice(invoice_id) do
    case Repo.get(Invoice, invoice_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  defp fetch_invoice_by_intent(intent_id) do
    case Repo.get_by(Invoice, stripe_payment_intent_id: intent_id) do
      nil -> {:error, :invoice_not_found}
      invoice -> {:ok, invoice}
    end
  end

  # `stripe_payment_intent_id` is left as-is on a decline (never
  # cleared) — its presence is what tells `CleanerCrmWeb.InvoiceLive.Show`
  # to offer "retry" instead of the initial "charge card" action.
  defp transition_invoice(%Invoice{} = invoice, new_status, payment_status) do
    Repo.transact(fn ->
      with {:ok, updated} <- invoice |> Invoice.changeset(%{status: new_status}) |> Repo.update() do
        update_payment_record(updated, payment_status)
        {:ok, updated}
      end
    end)
  end

  # The `Payment` submitted alongside the charge is normally still
  # `:pending` here and just gets its outcome filled in; a fixture-seeded
  # invoice (no prior `charge_card/2` call) has none, so one is created
  # for the audit trail.
  defp update_payment_record(%Invoice{} = invoice, status) do
    case Repo.get_by(Payment,
           invoice_id: invoice.id,
           stripe_payment_intent_id: invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id
         ) do
      nil -> record_payment(invoice, invoice.stripe_payment_intent_id, "webhook", status)
      payment -> payment |> Payment.changeset(%{status: status}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.Billing.Invoice do
  @moduledoc """
  An invoice for a completed job.

  Per the payments-stripe ADR, `status` only ever advances on a Stripe
  webhook confirmation: charging a card or sending a payment link just
  submits a charge and moves the invoice to `:charge_pending`; only the
  webhook marks it `:paid`, and a declined charge reverts it to
  `:unpaid` so the owner can retry or fall back to a payment link.
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @type status :: :unpaid | :charge_pending | :paid

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          amount_cents: integer() | nil,
          status: status(),
          stripe_payment_intent_id: String.t() | nil,
          payment_token: String.t() | nil,
          job: CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job.t() | Ecto.Association.NotLoaded.t(),
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "invoices" do
    field :amount_cents, :integer
    field :amount, :decimal, virtual: true
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :charge_pending, :paid], default: :unpaid
    field :stripe_payment_intent_id, :string
    field :payment_token, :string

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(job_id amount amount_cents status stripe_payment_intent_id payment_token)a

  def changeset(invoice, attrs) do
    invoice
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id])
    |> put_amount_cents()
    # After `put_amount_cents/1`, not before — a caller supplying dollars
    # via `amount` has no `amount_cents` yet until that step runs.
    # Needed because `validate_number/3` below only runs against an
    # actual *change*, so an explicit `amount_cents: nil` (unchanged from
    # a fresh `%Invoice{}`'s own default) silently skips it and would
    # otherwise reach `amount_cents`'s NOT NULL column as a raised
    # constraint violation instead of a changeset error.
    |> validate_required([:amount_cents])
    |> validate_number(:amount_cents, greater_than_or_equal_to: 0)
    |> unique_constraint(:payment_token)
  end

  # `amount` arrives as dollars (a `Decimal`, matching the money-handling
  # ADR); rounded half-up and stored as `amount_cents` — the only column
  # ever persisted. Callers that already have cents (e.g. copying a job's
  # `agreed_price_cents`) pass `amount_cents` directly and skip this.
  defp put_amount_cents(changeset) do
    case get_change(changeset, :amount) do
      nil ->
        changeset

      %Decimal{} = amount ->
        cents = amount |> Decimal.mult(100) |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up) |> Decimal.to_integer()
        put_change(changeset, :amount_cents, cents)
    end
  end
end

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings do
  @moduledoc """
  Pure pay calculations — no scope, no `Repo`. Given a job and its
  time entries, this is the only place clocked time (or a fixed piece
  rate) turns into cents.
  """

  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.TimeEntry

  @doc "Seconds between clock-in and clock-out. Only meaningful once resolved."
  def worked_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_in_at: in_at, clocked_out_at: out_at})
      when not is_nil(out_at) do
    DateTime.diff(out_at, in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed so far on a still-open entry."
  def elapsed_seconds(%TimeEntry{clocked_out_at: nil, clocked_in_at: in_at}) do
    DateTime.diff(DateTime.utc_now(), in_at, :second)
  end

  @doc """
  Cents earned on a job given its (possibly empty) list of time
  entries: the flat piece rate regardless of time for a piece-rate job
  — shown even before the cleaner has started, since it doesn't
  depend on any entry existing — or the hourly rate times total
  resolved worked time. `nil` when an hourly job has no resolved
  entries yet, or a job carries neither pay type: there's nothing to
  compute pay from, and it must not be silently priced at $0.
  """
  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :piece_rate, piece_rate_cents: cents}, _entries)
      when is_integer(cents) do
    cents
  end

  def job_cents(%Job{pay_type: :hourly, hourly_rate_cents: rate}, entries)
      when is_integer(rate) and is_list(entries) and entries != [] do
    if Enum.all?(entries, &TimeEntry.resolved?/1) do
      entries |> Enum.map(&worked_seconds/1) |> Enum.sum() |> hourly_cents(rate)
    end
  end

  def job_cents(_job, _entries), do: nil

  defp hourly_cents(seconds, rate_cents) do
    Decimal.new(rate_cents)
    |> Decimal.mult(Decimal.div(Decimal.new(seconds), Decimal.new(3600)))
    |> Decimal.round(0, :half_up)
    |> Decimal.to_integer()
  end
end

1	defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
2	  @moduledoc """
3	  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
4	  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.
5	
6	  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
7	  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
8	  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
9	  """
10	
11	  import Ecto.Query, warn: false
12	
13	  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
14	  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
15	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
16	  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
17	  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
18	  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}
19	
20	  ## Clocking in and out
21	
22	  @doc """
23	  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
24	  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
25	  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
26	  somewhere else.
27	  """
28	  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
29	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
30	    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
31	         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
32	      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
33	    end
34	  end
35	
36	  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
37	  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
38	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
39	    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
40	      nil ->
41	        {:error, :not_clocked_in}
42	
43	      entry ->
44	        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
45	    end
46	  end
47	
48	  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
49	  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}
50	
51	  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
52	    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
53	      nil -> :ok
54	      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
55	      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
56	    end
57	  end
58	
59	  @doc """
60	  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
61	  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
62	  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
63	  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
64	  """
65	  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
66	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
67	    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))
68	
69	    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
70	    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
71	    |> Repo.insert()
72	  end
73	
74	  @doc """
75	  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
76	  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
77	  clock-out.
78	  """
79	  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
80	      when not is_nil(account_id) do
81	    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
82	         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
83	      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
84	    end
85	  end
86	
87	  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
88	    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
89	      {:ok, value} -> value
90	      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
91	    end
92	  end
93	
94	  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}
95	
96	  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
97	    case String.split(string, ":") do
98	      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
99	      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
100	    end
101	  end
102	
103	  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
104	  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
105	  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
106	  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
107	  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
108	  # forward to the next day instead.
109	  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
110	    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
111	
112	    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
113	      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
114	        {:ok, candidate}
115	      else
116	        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)

defmodule CleanerCrm.TimeTracking do
  @moduledoc """
  Clock-in/out per job, hourly and piece-rate pay, transparent
  per-job and pay-period earnings, and payroll-ready CSV export.

  Every function is scoped to the caller's active account. Money is
  always integer cents; `CleanerCrm.Money` formats it for display and
  `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings` does the cents math.
  """

  import Ecto.Query, warn: false

  alias CleanerCrm.Accounts
  alias CleanerCrm.Repo
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling
  alias CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job
  alias CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.{Earnings, PayRate, PayrollExport, TimeEntry}
  alias CleanerCrm.Users.{Scope, User}

  ## Clocking in and out

  @doc """
  Clocks the scope's user in to `job`. Fails closed: `{:error,
  :not_assigned}` if the job isn't theirs, `{:error,
  {:already_clocked_in, other_job}}` if they're still on the clock
  somewhere else.
  """
  def clock_in(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with :ok <- ensure_assigned(job, scope.user),
         :ok <- ensure_not_already_clocked_in(scope, job) do
      create_time_entry(scope, %{job_id: job.id, clocked_in_at: DateTime.utc_now()})
    end
  end

  @doc "Clocks the scope's user out of their open entry on `job`."
  def clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil ->
        {:error, :not_clocked_in}

      entry ->
        entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: DateTime.utc_now()}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp ensure_assigned(%Job{cleaner_id: cleaner_id}, %User{id: cleaner_id}), do: :ok
  defp ensure_assigned(_job, _user), do: {:error, :not_assigned}

  defp ensure_not_already_clocked_in(%Scope{user: user} = scope, %Job{id: job_id}) do
    case open_time_entry_for_cleaner(scope, user.id) do
      nil -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{job_id: ^job_id} -> :ok
      %TimeEntry{} = entry -> {:error, {:already_clocked_in, Repo.preload(entry, :job).job}}
    end
  end

  @doc """
  Creates a resolved (or open, if `clocked_out_at` is omitted or
  `nil`) time entry directly. The sanctioned bypass
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.time_entry_fixture` seeds through — real
  clock-in/out goes through `clock_in/2` and `clock_out/2` above.
  """
  def create_time_entry(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    job = Scheduling.get_job!(scope, fetch!(attrs, :job_id))

    %TimeEntry{account_id: account_id, job_id: job.id, cleaner_id: job.cleaner_id}
    |> TimeEntry.changeset(attrs)
    |> Repo.insert()
  end

  @doc """
  Sets the clock-out time on an open entry to a specific time of day
  on its clock-in date — how the owner resolves a forgotten
  clock-out.
  """
  def resolve_clock_out(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %TimeEntry{} = entry, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    with {:ok, time} <- parse_time(fetch!(attrs, :clock_out_time)),
         {:ok, clocked_out_at} <- combine(entry.clocked_in_at, time) do
      entry |> TimeEntry.changeset(%{clocked_out_at: clocked_out_at}) |> Repo.update()
    end
  end

  defp fetch!(attrs, key) do
    case Map.fetch(attrs, key) do
      {:ok, value} -> value
      :error -> Map.fetch!(attrs, to_string(key))
    end
  end

  defp parse_time(%Time{} = time), do: {:ok, time}

  defp parse_time(string) when is_binary(string) do
    case String.split(string, ":") do
      [_hour, _minute] -> Time.from_iso8601(string <> ":00")
      _ -> Time.from_iso8601(string)
    end
  end

  # Combines the submitted time-of-day with the clock-in's date. A
  # resolution submitted for the same day is the common case, but a
  # cleaner who clocked in late at night and got resolved the next
  # morning would otherwise land before their own clock-in and fail
  # validation — so a candidate that doesn't come after clock-in rolls
  # forward to the next day instead.
  defp combine(%DateTime{time_zone: time_zone} = clocked_in_at, %Time{} = time) do
    date = DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)

    with {:ok, candidate} <- DateTime.new(date, time, time_zone) do
      if DateTime.compare(candidate, clocked_in_at) == :gt do
        {:ok, candidate}
      else
        DateTime.new(Date.add(date, 1), time, time_zone)
      end
    end
  end

  ## Reading time entries

  def open_time_entry_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def open_time_entry_for_cleaner(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.cleaner_id == ^cleaner_id and is_nil(t.clocked_out_at)
    )
    |> order_by([t], desc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> limit(1)
    |> Repo.one()
  end

  def list_time_entries_for_job(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, %Job{} = job)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id and t.job_id == ^job.id)
    |> order_by([t], asc: t.clocked_in_at)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Earnings

  @doc """
  Cents earned on `job` so far — see `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking.Earnings.job_cents/2`
  for exactly what that means for each pay type.
  """
  def job_earnings_cents(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    Earnings.job_cents(job, list_time_entries_for_job(scope, job))
  end

  @doc "Seconds elapsed on the cleaner's currently-open entry for `job`, or `nil` if not clocked in."
  def elapsed_seconds(%Scope{} = scope, %Job{} = job) do
    case open_time_entry_for_job(scope, job) do
      nil -> nil
      entry -> Earnings.elapsed_seconds(entry)
    end
  end

  ## Pay periods

  @doc "The Monday-Sunday week containing `date`."
  def pay_period_for(%Date{} = date) do
    monday = Date.add(date, -(Date.day_of_week(date) - 1))
    {monday, Date.add(monday, 6)}
  end

  @doc """
  The account's current pay period: the week containing its most
  recent time entry, falling back to this real-world week when the
  account has none yet. Anchoring on the latest activity rather than
  the wall clock means newly-seeded or backfilled data is visible the
  moment the owner opens the timesheet, with no period picker to
  navigate first.
  """
  def current_pay_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}) when not is_nil(account_id) do
    TimeEntry
    |> where([t], t.account_id == ^account_id)
    |> select([t], max(t.clocked_in_at))
    |> Repo.one()
    |> case do
      nil -> Date.utc_today()
      clocked_in_at -> DateTime.to_date(clocked_in_at)
    end
    |> pay_period_for()
  end

  @doc """
  Every job with time recorded in `period` (a `{start_date, end_date}`
  tuple), with its cleaner, entries, earned cents (`nil` if
  unresolved), and resolved status — the timesheet's row-level data.
  """
  def list_job_time_summaries(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, {_, _} = period)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> time_entries_in_period(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.job_id)
    |> Enum.map(fn {_job_id, entries} ->
      job = hd(entries).job
      cents = Earnings.job_cents(job, entries)
      open? = Enum.any?(entries, &(!TimeEntry.resolved?(&1)))

      %{
        job: job,
        cleaner: job.cleaner,
        entries: entries,
        cents: cents,
        # `open?` is genuinely missing a clock-out — the only state a
        # clock-out resolution can fix. `unresolved?` is broader: it
        # also covers a job whose entries are all closed but whose pay
        # can't be computed yet (missing pay type/rate), which must
        # block payroll the same way an open entry does rather than
        # silently price at $0 — but has no open entry for a
        # clock-out resolution to act on, so the two are tracked
        # separately rather than folded into one flag.
        open?: open?,
        unresolved?: is_nil(cents) or open?
      }
    end)
    |> Enum.sort_by(& &1.job.scheduled_date, Date)
  end

  @doc """
  Per-cleaner totals for `period`, excluding unresolved jobs. A
  cleaner whose only job is unresolved still appears, at zero — the
  amount isn't missing, it's withheld pending resolution.
  """
  def cleaner_pay_totals(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    scope
    |> list_job_time_summaries(period)
    |> Enum.group_by(& &1.cleaner.id)
    |> Map.new(fn {cleaner_id, summaries} ->
      total = summaries |> Enum.reject(& &1.unresolved?) |> Enum.map(& &1.cents) |> Enum.sum()
      {cleaner_id, total}
    end)
  end

  defp time_entries_in_period(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, {start_date, end_date}) do
    start_at = DateTime.new!(start_date, ~T[00:00:00])
    end_at = DateTime.new!(Date.add(end_date, 1), ~T[00:00:00])

    TimeEntry
    |> where(
      [t],
      t.account_id == ^account_id and t.clocked_in_at >= ^start_at and t.clocked_in_at < ^end_at
    )
    |> preload(job: :cleaner)
    |> Repo.all()
  end

  ## Payroll export

  @doc """
  Exports `period`'s earnings to CSV, one row per cleaner. Refuses
  with `{:error, :unresolved_entries}` while any job in the period is
  still missing a clock-out — payroll never goes out on an estimate.
  """
  def export_pay_period_csv(%Scope{} = scope, period) do
    summaries = list_job_time_summaries(scope, period)

    if Enum.any?(summaries, & &1.unresolved?) do
      {:error, :unresolved_entries}
    else
      {:ok, PayrollExport.to_csv(summaries)}
    end
  end

  ## Drive-time policy

  @doc "The account's drive-time pay policy, for display alongside a cleaner's earnings."
  def drive_time_policy(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Accounts.get_account!(scope, account_id).drive_time_policy
  end

  ## Pay rates (per-cleaner defaults)

  def get_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id}, cleaner_id)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    Repo.get_by(PayRate, account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id)
  end

  def set_pay_rate(%Scope{active_account_id: account_id} = scope, cleaner_id, attrs)
      when not is_nil(account_id) do
    scope
    |> get_pay_rate(cleaner_id)
    |> Kernel.||(%PayRate{account_id: account_id, cleaner_id: cleaner_id})
    |> PayRate.changeset(Map.put(attrs, :cleaner_id, cleaner_id))
    |> Repo.insert_or_update()
  end
end

2	  @moduledoc """
3	  An outbound message — a client appointment reminder or a cleaner
4	  schedule-change alert — with delivery status and acknowledgment
5	  tracking.
6	
7	  `kind: :reminder` notifications carry a `client_id` and move through
8	  `:sent -> :delivered | :undelivered -> :confirmed | :reschedule_requested`.
9	  `kind: :schedule_change` notifications carry a `cleaner_id` instead
10	  and move through `:pending -> :acknowledged` (or `:escalated` when
11	  never acknowledged in time).
12	  """
13	
14	  use Ecto.Schema
15	  import Ecto.Changeset
16	
17	  @kinds [:reminder, :schedule_change]
18	  @channels [:email, :sms, :push]
19	  @statuses [
20	    :pending,
21	    :sent,
22	    :delivered,
23	    :undelivered,
24	    :failed,
25	    :confirmed,
26	    :reschedule_requested,
27	    :acknowledged,
28	    :escalated
29	  ]

defmodule CleanerCrm.Notifications.Notification do
  @moduledoc """
  An outbound message — a client appointment reminder or a cleaner
  schedule-change alert — with delivery status and acknowledgment
  tracking.

  `kind: :reminder` notifications carry a `client_id` and move through
  `:sent -> :delivered | :undelivered -> :confirmed | :reschedule_requested`.
  `kind: :schedule_change` notifications carry a `cleaner_id` instead
  and move through `:pending -> :acknowledged` (or `:escalated` when
  never acknowledged in time).
  """

  use Ecto.Schema
  import Ecto.Changeset

  @kinds [:reminder, :schedule_change]
  @channels [:email, :sms, :push]
  @statuses [
    :pending,
    :sent,
    :delivered,
    :undelivered,
    :failed,
    :confirmed,
    :reschedule_requested,
    :acknowledged,
    :escalated
  ]

  @type t :: %__MODULE__{
          id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          account_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          client_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          cleaner_id: integer() | nil,
          job_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil,
          kind: :reminder | :schedule_change,
          channel: :email | :sms | :push,
          status: atom(),
          token: String.t() | nil,
          provider_message_id: String.t() | nil,
          failure_reason: String.t() | nil,
          change_summary: String.t() | nil,
          pushed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          sent_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          delivered_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          confirmed_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          reschedule_requested_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          acknowledged_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          escalated_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          inserted_at: DateTime.t() | nil,
          updated_at: DateTime.t() | nil
        }

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "notifications" do
    field :kind, Ecto.Enum, values: @kinds
    field :channel, Ecto.Enum, values: @channels
    field :status, Ecto.Enum, values: @statuses, default: :pending
    field :token, :string
    field :provider_message_id, :string
    field :failure_reason, :string
    field :change_summary, :string

    field :pushed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :sent_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :delivered_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :confirmed_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :reschedule_requested_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :acknowledged_at, :utc_datetime_usec
    field :escalated_at, :utc_datetime_usec

    belongs_to :account, CleanerCrm.Accounts.Account, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :client, CleanerCrm.Clients.Client, type: :binary_id
    belongs_to :cleaner, CleanerCrm.Users.User
    belongs_to :job, CleanerCrm.Scheduling.Job, type: :binary_id

    timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)
  end

  @fields ~w(client_id cleaner_id job_id kind channel status token provider_message_id
             failure_reason change_summary pushed_at sent_at delivered_at confirmed_at
             reschedule_requested_at acknowledged_at escalated_at)a

  def changeset(notification, attrs) do
    notification
    |> cast(attrs, @fields)
    |> validate_required([:job_id, :kind, :channel, :token])
    |> unique_constraint(:token)
    |> foreign_key_constraint(:job_id)
  end

  def kinds, do: @kinds
  def channels, do: @channels
  def statuses, do: @statuses
end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7197Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7197 — Office sees who has not acknowledged

  The push itself is covered end-to-end by criteria 7190/7191; this
  spec's subject is the board's acknowledgment-status visibility, so
  the already-pending notification is seeded directly via
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture/4`.
  The scenario then re-drives the real acknowledge action on
  `FieldLive.Today` to observe the status flip on `ScheduleLive.Board`,
  since that flip is the criterion's own subject.

  Assumes the board shows a per-job acknowledgment-status control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-ack-status']`) rendering "Unacknowledged" or
  "Acknowledged".
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "the office sees per-job acknowledgment status flip as the cleaner acknowledges" do
    scenario "office sees who has not acknowledged" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "the office pushed a schedule change to a cleaner", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today()
          })

        notification =
          Fixtures.schedule_change_notification_fixture(context.scope, cleaner, job)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           cleaner: cleaner,
           cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn,
           job: job,
           notification: notification
         })}
      end

      given_ "the cleaner has not acknowledged it", context do
        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the office views the change", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :board_live, board_live)}
      end

      then_ "it shows as unacknowledged for that cleaner", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-ack-status']",
                 "Unacknowledged"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "the cleaner acknowledges the change", context do
        {:ok, today_live, _html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        today_live
        |> element("[data-test='schedule-alert-#{context.notification.id}-acknowledge-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "once the cleaner acknowledges, the office sees it flip to acknowledged", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-ack-status']",
                 "Acknowledged"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

  @reserved_slugs ~w(admin api www help support docs blog)

  @primary_key {:id, :binary_id, autogenerate: true}
  schema "accounts" do
    field :name, :string
    field :slug, :string

    # Whether time spent driving between jobs counts toward a
    # cleaner's pay — read by `CleanerCrm.TimeTracking` alongside a
    # cleaner's earnings, set here rather than on a separate settings
    # table since it's the account's only pay policy so far.
    field :drive_time_policy, Ecto.Enum, values: [:unpaid, :paid], default: :unpaid

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story843.Criterion7191Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 843 — Get loud, acknowledged alerts when my schedule changes
  Criterion 7191 — Cancelling a job on the schedule board pushes the
  assigned cleaner a notification that the job was cancelled.

  Assumes the board exposes a per-job cancel control
  (`[data-test='job-<id>-cancel-button']`, `phx-click="cancel_job"`).
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a cancelled job notifies the assigned cleaner" do
    scenario "cancelled job notifies the cleaner" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have a job scheduled for later today", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.utc_today(),
            start_time: ~T[16:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[17:30:00]
          })

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{cleaner: cleaner, cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn, job: job})}
      end

      when_ "the office cancels that job", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        board_live
        |> element("[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-cancel-button']")
        |> render_click()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I receive a notification that the job has been cancelled", context do
        {:ok, today_live, html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        assert has_element?(today_live, "[data-test='schedule-alert']")
        assert html =~ "Cancelled"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

    |> Phoenix.ConnTest.init_test_session(%{})
    |> Plug.Conn.put_session(:portal_client_id, client.id)
  end

  end

        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story851.Criterion7225Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 851 — Reschedule or cancel a visit within the policy
  Criterion 7225 — Reschedule notifies office and cleaner

  A portal reschedule is expected to push the same `:schedule_change`
  notification kind story 843's board-driven reschedule does (route
  contract: "changes create schedule-change notifications (existing
  Notifications context) for the assigned cleaner"), so this reuses
  the observation points criteria 7190 and 7197 already establish:
  the cleaner's `[data-test='schedule-alert']` on `FieldLive.Today`,
  and the office's `[data-test='job-<id>-ack-status']` on
  `ScheduleLive.Board`.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "rescheduling from the portal notifies the assigned cleaner and shows the office it's unacknowledged" do
    scenario "reschedule notifies office and cleaner" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have an upcoming visit assigned to a cleaner", context do
        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{
            email: "cleaner-#{System.unique_integer([:positive])}@example.com"
          })

        cleaner_conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn(), cleaner)
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        job =
          Fixtures.job_fixture(context.scope, client, %{
            cleaner_id: cleaner.id,
            scheduled_date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7),
            start_time: ~T[13:00:00],
            end_time: ~T[14:30:00]
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           cleaner: cleaner,
           cleaner_conn: cleaner_conn,
           client: client,
           job: job,
           portal_conn: portal_conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "I reschedule the visit to a new time", context do
        {:ok, visit_live, _html} =
          live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/visits/#{context.job.id}")

        visit_live
        |> form("[data-test='reschedule-form']",
          visit: %{date: Date.add(Date.utc_today(), 7), start_time: "15:00"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the assigned cleaner receives a schedule-change alert", context do
        {:ok, today_live, html} = live(context.cleaner_conn, ~p"/field")

        assert has_element?(today_live, "[data-test='schedule-alert']")
        assert html =~ "1:00 PM"
        assert html =~ "3:00 PM"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the office sees it as unacknowledged on the schedule board", context do
        {:ok, board_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/schedule")

        assert has_element?(
                 board_live,
                 "[data-test='job-#{context.job.id}-ack-status']",
                 "Unacknowledged"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

1:# Mix.Tasks.Spex
3:Run spex files - executable specifications for AI-driven development.
5:SexySpex provides a framework for writing executable specifications that serve as
6:both tests and living documentation, optimized for AI-driven development workflows.
8:Each spex file manages its own application lifecycle using setup_all and setup blocks:
9:- setup_all: Application startup and shutdown
10:- setup: State reset between tests
11:- Context passing between test steps
12:- Integration with external tools (like ScenicMCP for GUI testing)
14:## Usage
16:    mix spex                    # Run all spex files
17:    mix spex path/to/file.exs   # Run specific spex file
18:    mix spex --help             # Show this help
20:## Options
22:    --pattern       File pattern to match (default: test/spex/**/*_spex.exs)
23:    --verbose       Show detailed spex Reporter output (quiet by default)
24:    --timeout       Test timeout in milliseconds (default: 60000)
25:    --manual        Interactive manual mode - step through each action
26:    --speed         Execution speed: fast (default), medium, slow
27:    --trace         Enable ExUnit trace mode (shows test execution details)
28:    --slowest N     Print timing information for the N slowest tests
29:    --formatter     ExUnit formatter module (default: ExUnit.CLIFormatter)
30:                    Can be specified multiple times
31:    --jsonl [PATH]  Output failures as JSONL (default: spex_failures.jsonl)
32:    --stale         Only run spex files that have changed or reference changed modules
33:    --force         Force all spex files to run (use with --stale to reset)
35:## Examples
37:    mix spex
38:    mix spex test/spex/user_login_spex.exs
39:    mix spex --pattern "**/integration_*_spex.exs"
40:    mix spex --verbose
41:    mix spex --manual           # Interactive step-by-step mode
42:    mix spex --speed slow       # Slower automatic execution
43:    mix spex --speed medium --verbose  # Medium speed with detailed output
44:    mix spex --trace            # Show detailed test execution
45:    mix spex test/spex/file.exs --trace
46:    mix spex --slowest 5        # Show timing for 5 slowest tests
48:## Configuration
50:You can configure spex behavior in your config files:
52:    config :sexy_spex,
53:      manual_mode: false,
54:      step_delay: 0
56:Application lifecycle is handled in individual spex files using setup_all blocks.
58:## Important: Test Environment Setup
60:To ensure spex runs in the test environment with proper module compilation,
61:add this to your project's mix.exs:
63:    def project do
64:      [
65:        # ... other config
66:        preferred_cli_env: [
67:          spex: :test
68:        ]
69:      ]
70:    end
72:This ensures that `mix spex` always runs in the test environment and compiles
73:modules with test-specific code paths (e.g., test/support directories).

# Write BDD Specs: Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal

**Story ID**: 852
**Description**: As a cleaning client, I want to view and pay invoices in the portal, manage my card on file, and add a digital tip that reaches my cleaner, so that payment never needs a phone call and tipping doesn't need cash. (Research: over half of tips are digital and incumbents track tips poorly — an in-portal tip prompt is a customer convenience and a cleaner-retention lever — customer-side.md §1; owner-side payment pains pain-points §1.8)
**Component**: `CleanerCrmWeb.PortalLive` (live_context)

## What you're producing

These are specifications of acceptance criteria, not regression tests
of existing behavior. A scenario is a mechanical translation of the
criterion text into Given/When/Then driving the real surface — what
the criterion **says must be true**, not what the code happens to do
today.

**Failing on first run is the expected outcome.** Unsatisfied criteria
produce red specs; the next workflow step uses that red bar to drive
the implementation. You do **not** need the scenarios to pass for
this task to succeed.

**The evaluator is shape-only** — it parses, compiles, asserts
`use *.Spex.Case`, and asserts Given/When/Then steps exist. It does
**not** run `mix test`. Validation passing is not the same as
scenarios passing. Encode the criterion faithfully; let the implementer
worry about turning it green.

## Required reading — both layers

Read both knowledge layers before writing specs. **Project rules
override framework rules where they conflict.**

### Framework BDD knowledge (read via the `read_knowledge` MCP tool, under `bdd/spex/`)

- `bdd/spex/writing_a_spex.md` — file layout, module template, DSL
  syntax, step return values. **Essential — read first.**
- `bdd/spex/philosophy.md` — what Spex is and how it differs from
  regular tests.
- `bdd/spex/environment.md` — environment abstraction in steps.
- `bdd/spex/boundaries.md` — what `given_` / `when_` / `then_` can and
  can't do.
- `bdd/spex/shared_givens.md` — importing shared given blocks.
- `bdd/spex/recording_cassettes.md` — when and how to record HTTP
  cassettes.

### Project BDD knowledge (`.code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/`)

- `four_surfaces_quick_reference.md` — the four interaction surfaces
  in this codebase (MCP tool, HTTP, LiveView, filesystem) with
  one-line "I'm testing X → use surface Y" table and 30-second
  skeletons. **Read second.**
- `surfaces.md` — canonical skeletons per surface, deeper detail.
- `cassettes.md` — project-specific cassette conventions.

## Component under test

Source: `lib/cleaner_crm_web/portal_live.ex` (couldn't read — open the file before writing specs to see the public API)

## Likely surface for this component

This component is a **live_context**. The most likely surface is
**LiveView (a user interacting with a page)**.

Pick by what the user (engineer or agent) would actually do, not by
component type alone — see
`.code_my_spec/knowledge/bdd/spex/four_surfaces_quick_reference.md`
for the full decision table and the 30-second skeleton.

## Acceptance criteria

### Criterion 7237: Client views invoice list

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/852_pay_invoices_and_tip_my_cleaner_from_the_portal/criterion_7237_client_views_invoice_list_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7238: Client pays an invoice with a new card

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/852_pay_invoices_and_tip_my_cleaner_from_the_portal/criterion_7238_client_pays_an_invoice_with_a_new_card_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7239: Invoice marked paid on webhook confirmation

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/852_pay_invoices_and_tip_my_cleaner_from_the_portal/criterion_7239_invoice_marked_paid_on_webhook_confirmation_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7240: Declined card leaves invoice unpaid

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/852_pay_invoices_and_tip_my_cleaner_from_the_portal/criterion_7240_declined_card_leaves_invoice_unpaid_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7241: Client saves a card on file

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/852_pay_invoices_and_tip_my_cleaner_from_the_portal/criterion_7241_client_saves_a_card_on_file_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7242: Client adds a tip at payment

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/852_pay_invoices_and_tip_my_cleaner_from_the_portal/criterion_7242_client_adds_a_tip_at_payment_spex.exs`

### Criterion 7243: Client pays without tipping

**Expected file path**: `test/spex/852_pay_invoices_and_tip_my_cleaner_from_the_portal/criterion_7243_client_pays_without_tipping_spex.exs`

## Procedure

Write **one** spec file per criterion, then **stop** for validation.
The evaluator runs after each session — it checks file existence,
parses, compiles via `Code.string_to_quoted/2`, asserts `use` of
`CleanerCrmSpex.Case`, and asserts at least one scenario with
Given/When/Then steps. If validation fails, next-session feedback
tells you exactly what's wrong.

For each criterion:

1. Create the spec file at the path shown above.
2. Module name under the `CleanerCrmSpex` namespace.
3. `use CleanerCrmSpex.Case` (NOT `<App>Web.ConnCase` directly —
   the case template wires up SexySpex + ConnTest + LiveViewTest +
   DB sandbox).
4. Drive the real interaction surface from `given_` / `when_` /
   `then_` steps. Never call context functions or `Repo` directly.
   Never read the DB from `then_`.
5. Run `mix compile` to verify.
6. **Stop and wait for validation** before starting the next spec.

## Do not

Failure modes that turn the spec into a self-fulfilling pass instead
of a faithful encoding of the criterion:

- **Soften the assertion to match current behavior.** If the criterion
  says 401, assert 401 — not `assert conn.status in [200, 401]`
  because the code returns 200 today.
- **Fabricate rules or criteria.** Only write scenarios for the rules
  and criteria already on the story. If something feels
  under-specified, surface the question — don't invent a rule.
- **`@tag :pending`, `@tag :skip`, or comment out scenarios that
  fail.** A failing scenario is the point. Tagging it out hides the
  signal the implementer needs.
- **Pre-seed in `given_` what the SUT should produce.** If the
  criterion says "creating a Foo also creates a Bar", `when_`
  triggers the action and `then_` asserts both side effects.
  Don't `given_` the Bar into existence.
- **Stub or mock the surface under test.** Drive the real LiveView /
  HTTP / MCP tool. Mocks make the spec a tautology.
- **Read the implementation and write its current behavior as the
  expectation.** Read the criterion; write the criterion. If the
  code doesn't match, that's information — surface it through a
  failing spec.

If a criterion is genuinely untestable, contradicts another, or is
ambiguous, **stop and flag it** rather than fudging the spec to fit.

- Case template: `test/support/cleaner_crm_spex_case.ex` — defines
  `CleanerCrmSpex.Case`.
- Boundary: `test/spex/cleaner_crm_spex.ex`.
- Shared givens: `test/support/shared_givens.ex`.

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story836.Criterion7155Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 836 — Invoice completed jobs and collect payment
  Criterion 7155 — Client with no card on file pays via payment link

  As in criterion 7154, job completion and invoice generation are
  seeded via `CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures` (covered end-to-end by
  criterion 7153) so this spec can focus on the payment-link
  collection path.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "collecting payment via a payment link when no card is on file" do
    scenario "client with no card on file pays via payment link" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{conn: conn, user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "a client has no card on file", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{card_on_file: false})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client, client)}
      end

      given_ "an invoice exists for that client's completed job", context do
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, context.client)
        invoice = Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{amount: job.agreed_price})

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job: job, invoice: invoice})}
      end

      when_ "the owner sends the invoice as a payment link and the client pays it online",
            context do
        {:ok, invoice_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/invoices/#{context.invoice.id}")

        html_after_send =
          invoice_live
          |> element("[data-test='send-payment-link-button']")
          |> render_click()

        [_, payment_path] = Regex.run(~r{href="(/pay/[^"]+)"}, html_after_send)

        client_conn =
          Phoenix.ConnTest.build_conn()
          |> post(payment_path, %{"payment_method" => "pm_card_visa", "save_card" => "true"})

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :client_conn, client_conn)}
      end

      then_ "the invoice is collected", context do
        assert Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.client_conn, 200) =~ "Payment received"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the client's card can be saved for next time", context do
        assert Phoenix.ConnTest.html_response(context.client_conn, 200) =~ "save your card"

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end

        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)
        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(context.conn, user)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story852.Criterion7238Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 852 — Pay invoices and tip my cleaner from the portal
  Criterion 7238 — Client pays an invoice with a new card

  Per the payments-stripe ADR (see `CleanerCrm.Billing`'s moduledoc),
  a submitted charge only ever moves an invoice to `:charge_pending`
  — final `:paid` status is webhook-driven (criterion 7239). This
  spec's subject is the submission itself, so it asserts the
  submission's own confirmation and receipt rather than a final
  "Paid" status.
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import Swoosh.TestAssertions

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a client pays an invoice with a new card from the portal" do
    scenario "client pays an invoice with a new card" do
      given_ "the owner is logged in with an active account", context do
        user = Fixtures.user_fixture()
        scope = Fixtures.user_scope_fixture(user)
        account = Fixtures.account_fixture(scope)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{user: user, scope: scope, account: account})}
      end

      given_ "I have an unpaid invoice and no card on file", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope, %{card_on_file: false})
        job = Fixtures.job_with_proof_of_work_fixture(context.scope, client)

        invoice =
          Fixtures.invoice_fixture(context.scope, job, %{
            amount: Decimal.new("150.00"),
            status: :unpaid
          })

        portal_conn = Fixtures.portal_session_fixture(client)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{client: client, invoice: invoice, portal_conn: portal_conn})}
      end

      when_ "I pay the invoice with a new card", context do
        {:ok, invoices_live, _html} = live(context.portal_conn, ~p"/portal/invoices")

        invoices_live
        |> element("[data-test='invoice-#{context.invoice.id}-pay-button']")
        |> render_click()

        invoices_live
        |> form("[data-test='invoice-#{context.invoice.id}-payment-form']",
          payment: %{card_token: "pm_card_visa"}
        )
        |> render_submit()

        {:ok, Map.put(context, :invoices_live, invoices_live)}
      end

      then_ "my payment is submitted for the full invoice amount", context do
        assert render(context.invoices_live) =~ "$150.00"

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "I receive a receipt", context do
        assert_email_sent(to: context.client.email)

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
